article_text:
Il 27 ottobre, nel pieno della Hong Kong Asian Art Week , Christie’s presenta una serie di opere eccezionali provenienti da importanti collezioni private, realizzate da artisti celebri nell’arco di diversi secoli. L’asta porta il nome di Fine Chinese Classical Paintings and Calligraphy e propone una raffinata selezione di opere rare e importanti, che abbracciano secoli di produzione artistica cinese.

A guidare la vendita è il lotto 655: un album di dodici fogli, The Lotus Garden: The Art and Provenance of Flowers and Birds Album di Bada Shanren , proveniente da una prestigiosa collezione privata. Shanren dipinse l’album all’inizio della primavera del 1699, all’età di settantatré anni, quando aveva raggiunto il culmine della propria maturità artistica. Passato attraverso diverse collezioni l’album fu esposto in Giappone, Taiwan e negli Stati Uniti e rappresenta uno dei più raffinati esempi superstiti della produzione tarda di Bada Shanren nel genere della pittura di fiori e uccelli. Le sue opere di Shanren appaiono essenziali e distaccate, ma sotto la superficie austera trasmettono sentimenti di grande profondità: l’album raffigura fiori, uccelli, pesci e rocce con una straordinaria semplicità. La maestria di Bada nell’utilizzo degli spazi vuoti permette a ogni soggetto di dominare il proprio universo poetico. Poche pennellate eppure i dettagli immergono l’osservatore nelle scene rappresentate, particolarmente suggestivi sono i suoi uccelli dagli occhi rivolti verso l’alto, i cui sguardi laterali sembrano esprimere un consapevole distacco dal mondo terreno.

Birds and Flowers (lotto 609) di Wang Liben con una stima HKD 1,600,000 – HKD 3,000,000 è una coppia di rotoli verticali in seta, un tempo conservati nella collezione dello shogunato Ashikaga in Giappone: in seguito all’instaurazione di relazioni ufficiali tra il Giappone e la corte cinese dei Ming, lo shogunato, in particolare sotto Ashikaga Yoshimitsu (1358–1408), costituì un’importante collezione di opere d’arte cinesi. Diversi secoli più tardi, entrarono a far parte della collezione di Shozo Kawasaki (1836–1912), imprenditore del periodo Meiji (1868–1912) un barone noto non solo per i suoi successi nell’industria e nel commercio, ma anche per la sua raffinata collezione. Nel 1890 istituì un museo privato, il Chōshunkaku , destinato a ospitare ed esporre oltre 2.000 opere d’arte, tra cui calligrafie e dipinti cinesi, porcellane e sculture in giada. Questa coppia di dipinti rimase nella Collezione Kawasaki fino a quando fu ceduta dopo una mostra tenutasi nel 1936.

Tra gli altri importanti lotti figurano anche Pine Trees and Calligraphy di Shen Zhou , già appartenuto alla collezione imperiale della dinastia Qing e Six Verses in Cursive Script di Wang Duo opera che comprende sei poesie di cinque caratteri, per un totale di 56 righe e 292 caratteri, titoli compresi. I componimenti esprimono il senso di angoscia e le frustrazioni politiche dell’autore in un periodo di profondo tumulto storico, segnato dal crollo della dinastia Ming e dalla violenta transizione verso la dinastia Qing.

Tra i punti salienti figurano inoltre i Poems in Running Script di Wen Zhengming e Poems for Emperor Qianlong’s Eightieth Birthday Celebration di Peng Yuanrui confermando un patrimonio che, torna a essere protagonista nella scena artistica.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Abramorama has acquired North American distribution rights to Make Work , the documentary commissioned by the New York Choreographic Institute (the Institute) and directed by two-time Emmy-nominated filmmakers Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger ( Restless Creature: Wendy Whelan ) and produced by Saffire, Schlesinger and Adrian Danchig-Waring.

The North American theatrical release is being lined up for March 5, 2027. The film will play at next month’s Doc NYC.

Set inside the studios and stages of The Institute and New York City Ballet, Make Work “offers rare, intimate access to the creative process behind contemporary ballet. The film follows four choreographers, Harrison Ball, Sarah Foster-Sproull, Caili Quan and Houston Thomas, as they develop new work with NYCB dancers, revealing the pressure, experimentation, collaboration and uncertainty that take place before a ballet reaches the stage. With only two weeks to create original work during the Institute’s residencies, the choreographers navigate the delicate balance between honoring ballet’s traditions and pushing against its boundaries.”

Related Stories

Abramorama Takes North America Rights, Sets Release For John David Coles Doc 'The Choice'

Director Rory Kennedy On 'The Trial Of Alec Baldwin,' And Why 'Rust' Star At First Reacted Negatively To Her Film

Interwoven are reflections from leading choreographers Kyle Abraham, Lar Lubovitch, Annabelle Lopez Ochoa, Justin Peck, Alexei Ratmansky, Pam Tanowitz and Christopher Wheeldon, who share perspectives on their creative practices and the enduring influence of George Balanchine on New York City Ballet and the evolution of ballet itself.

Watch on Deadline

The announcement comes as Danchig-Waring took his final bow with NYCB on Sunday, October 18, 2026, during a farewell performance marking the conclusion of his more than 24 years with the company. In the film, Danchig-Waring, who serves as a producer on Make Work and as Artistic Director of the New York Choreographic Institute, NYCB’s hub of creativity, gives his perspective on the institution and the artists working to shape its future.

Saffire and Schlesinger previously co-directed and produced Restless Creature: Wendy Whelan , which premiered at the New York Film Festival and was released by Netflix, and Sporting Dreams. They also co-produced Smash His Camera , which won Best Director at the Sundance Film Festival. Schlesinger’s producing credits include Ai Weiwei: Never Sorry , which received the Sundance Special Jury Prize and was shortlisted for an Academy Award, as well as Page One: Inside the New York Times and God Grew Tired of Us , winner of both the Audience Award and Grand Jury Prize at Sundance.

“We’ve always been drawn to the moments audiences never get to see,” said co-directors Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger. “With Make Work , we wanted to sit in the room while a ballet is being born, when ideas are fragile, when dancers and choreographers are taking real risks together, and when failure is part of the process. What we found was an art form deeply rooted in Balanchine’s legacy and fiercely committed to reinventing itself. These choreographers are asking what ballet can be, and who it can be for, and we hope the film lets audiences feel what it takes to answer that question.”

“For more than two decades, New York City Ballet has been my home, and the studio has been where I’ve learned the most about what it means to be an artist,” said Adrian Danchig-Waring. “The Institute exists to give choreographers the time, space and trust to experiment, and to fail, and that is where the future of ballet is being written. Make Work honors that process and the courageous artists who are shaping ballet’s next chapter.”

“ Make Work gives audiences a rare and intimate window into the creative process at one of the world’s most influential ballet institutions,” said Karol Martesko-Fenster, CEO of AB2 Media Group / Abramorama, and Damon G. Smith, SVP of Business Growth and Creative Strategy. “The film captures something universal about making art — the uncertainty, the risk, the collaboration and ultimately the courage required to create something that has never existed before.”

article_text:
Announcement

New Art Books from the Quarto Group

From art history to instruction, Quarto publishes visually-rich books for artists of all mediums and skill levels.

Quarto publishes visually-rich books for artists of all mediums and skill levels. Explore highlights from the 2026 collection!

Light & Color in the Watercolor Landscape

By Vladislav Yeliseyev Discover the secrets to capturing depth, atmosphere, and emotion in your watercolor landscapes with Light and Color in the Watercolor Landscape . Acclaimed artist and instructor Vladislav Yeliseyev shares his proven techniques for harnessing light and shadow, creating luminous colors, and refining compositions to enhance realism and impact.

Frida Kahlo at Home

By Suzanne Barbezat Discover the intimate spaces that shaped one of the world’s most iconic artists. This compelling visual biography traces Kahlo’s life through the places she loved, from her childhood in Coyoacán and her student years in Mexico City, to her time in the United States, and her final return to La Casa Azul. Drawing on archival photographs, family images, personal artefacts, and Frida’s own paintings, the book uncovers how home was not merely a backdrop but a central force in her art and self‑expression.

New Lessons in Landscape Painting

By Mitchell Albala Refine and expand your landscape painting skills with this next-level guide by award-winning painter and bestselling author Mitchell Albala. New Lessons in Landscape Painting builds on the success of the bestselling The Landscape Painter’s Workbook , with new topics, step-by-step exercises, demonstrations, and in-depth painting analyses. Each is designed to build stronger skills in the core practices of landscape painting: shape interpretation, composition, and color.

The Wild Magic of Iceland

By Norris Niman For centuries, the breathtaking waterfalls, fierce volcanoes, and sweeping green hills of Iceland have captivated travelers’ imaginations. In The Wild Magic of Iceland , acclaimed photographer and adventurer Norris Niman transports you to these and more picturesque sites on a visual adventure through the seasons, featuring 100+ dazzling photographs.

Paul Nicklen: A Photography Masterclass

By Paul Nicklen Join Paul Nicklen – renowned conservationist, wildlife and art photographer – for a rare, tell-all masterclass in photography. Drawing on more than three decades of experience, including 20 years of shooting for National Geographic, Nicklen distils his craft into 20 key lessons, each with a clear and simple takeaway.

Art of the New York Subway

By Adrian Brune Step into the world’s largest underground art museum with Art of the New York Subway , a stunning tribute to the artistry that transforms the New York subway from a transit system into a cultural landmark. Tracing nearly 200 stations of the subway, this book celebrates the fusion of architecture, design and public art that defines New York’s identity.

Wanderlust Ink

By Ollie Smither Wanderlust Ink is a stunning collection of fine-line tattoo designs that amaze and inspire. These thoughtful, hand-drawn designs by popular artist and designer Ollie Smither (@os.illustration) demonstrate a passion for travel, adventure, nature, and connectivity of all kinds.

The Art of the Unknown

By S. Elizabeth The Art of the Unknown is an enthralling journey for anyone fascinated by mystery and the esoteric, inviting you to look again at the forces that persist just beyond the threshold of ordinary reality, and to discover how artists have long attempted to make the invisible visible.

Learn more at quarto.com

article_text:
港区の文化芸術の中核施設として期待膨らむ

2027年11月に「港区立みなと芸術センターｍ∼ｍ（むーむ）」（東京都港区浜松町）が開館します。約600席の客席のあるプロセニアム形式のシアターや、公演やワークショップ、稽古など多目的に使えるコモンスペース、スタジオやアトリエなどを備え、東京都心の港区における文化芸術の中核施設として期待されています。

浜松町駅の駅前通路から直結

JR・東京モノレールの浜松町駅の駅前通路から直結とアクセスも便利です。愛称「ｍ∼ｍ（むーむ）」は公募で選ばれ、「minato（みなと）」と「me(わたし）」の結びつき、「無」から生み出す「無限大」の可能性などを表しています。

多彩なメニューのプロローグ・イベント

国際都市・港区の文化の“顔”となる同センターの開館を1年後に控え、港区は2026年11月28日(土)に浜松町コンベンションホールで「開館１年前 プロローグ・イベント」を開催します。入場無料。事前申し込みが必要なプログラムがあります。申し込みは現在受付中で、先着順のプログラムや、申込期間を設けて応募多数の場合は抽選を行うプログラムもあります。詳細は みなと芸術センターホームページ より確認ください。

当日は、ゲストの濱田祐太郎さん（お笑い芸人）・深田晃司さん（映画監督）・藤間爽子さん（俳優・日本舞踊家）と港区長によるトーク、落語、漫談、港区で生まれた物語についての特別対談、ろう者も聴者も子ども大人も参加可能なワークショップ、開館予定のm∼ｍを遊戯的に体験できるVR、アーティストと浜松町を巡るウォーキングツアーなど、子どもから大人まで楽しめる様々なプログラムを企画しています。概要と主なイベントを以下に紹介します。

「開館１年前 プロローグ・イベント」

日程：2026年11月28日（土）

会場：浜松町コンベンションホール （港区浜松町2-3-1 日本生命浜松町クレアタワー5F）

入場料：無料

主催：港区

企画制作・問合せ先：みなと芸術センター開館準備室 03—6809—3631（平日9:30-17:00）

「開館１年前 プロローグ・イベント」詳細ページ： https://www.minatoartscenter.jp/topic/2690/

■プログラム一覧 １．[トーク＆パフォーマンス] 『m∼mをめぐる語りの共演』 ３部にわたり、漫談、落語、トークなどを通して、m∼mが目指す姿を感じていただくひとときです。 第１部 ［漫 談］ 濱田祐太郎（お笑い芸人） 第２部 ［トーク］ 濱田祐太郎、深田晃司（映画監督）、藤間爽子（俳優・日本舞踊家）、清家愛（港区長） 第３部 ［落語×手話］ 桂福壱（手話落語家）、三遊亭遊雀（落語家） ２．[特別対談] 木ノ下裕一×都倉武之『物語の生まれる場所へ～港区編』 港区では歴史的にどんな物語が生まれてきたのか？地域と物語・歴史の関係を探る特別対談。 ３．[VRエンターテインメント] 谷口勝也『バーチャルｍ∼ｍ Version 2.0』 みなと芸術センターm∼mのイメージを、一足先にVR（バーチャル・リアリティ）で体験。 ４．[ワークショップ] めとてラボ『ことばのあいだで、物語をつくろう！』 音声や文字、手話など、さまざまな「ことば」から物語をつくるワークショップ。 ５．[ウォーキングツアー] SIDE CORE『Looking from inside outside』 浜松町駅を起点に港区湾岸地域のこれまでとこれからを感じるウォーキングツアー。 ６．[砂浜スペース] 予約不要・出入自由。砂浜をイメージした空間で、いつでも休憩したり、遊んだり、気ままに過ごせます。 ７．[砂浜コンサート] 予約不要・出入自由。石上真由子（ヴァイオリン）と水野優也（チェロ）によるミニ・コンサート。 （美術展ナビ編集班）

article_text:
10月30日〜11月3日、杉並・early spring gallery & shopにて、IACKが出版する初作品集『2026.6.22 13:30‒15:21』の刊行を記念したイベントとIACKポップアップストアが開催される。

本書は、5月16日〜6月22日に青森市で開催された展覧会「到来について」（発起人：龍崎俊・宇田川直寛、共同企画：河野幸人）を起点に生まれた一冊。旧カラオケ店の空きテナントビル全体を使ったこのグループ展では、「この世界から写真がなくなったら？」という問いのもと、相ヶ瀬広大、天野祐子、宇田川直寛、コイズミアヤ、河野幸人、高原颯時、田中藍衣、對木裕里、野田幸江、益永梢子、山口幸士、龍崎俊の12名が、さまざまな形態の作品を発表された。

作品集は、展覧会最終日に河野が撮影した映像のキャプチャによって構成されている。展覧会の忠実な記録でも、展示を事後的に美化するための本でもなく、ひとりの人物がビルの階段を3階まで上り、そして会場を後にする──その移動を通じて、作品とともに、会場となった建物の独特なつくりや空間も映し出しているという。映像から切り出したイメージと本の形式を用いて、展示コンセプトを引き継ぐ形でアーカイブの可能性を探っている。

また会期の10月31日には、龍崎俊・宇田川直寛・河野幸人によるトークイベントが予定されており、同日夜には音楽活動も行う河野と、スウェーデンを拠点に活動する英国出身のミュージシャン、ジョン・コリンによるライブも行われる。秋の夜長にぜひ足を運んで愉しみたい。

イベント

『2026.6.22 13:30‒15:21』刊行記念イベント ＆ IACK POP UP STORE

場所

early spring gallery & shop （〒168-0063 東京都杉並区和泉3丁目30-8）

title_original: Paris Photo 2026: imparare a guardare attraverso gli occhi degli altri
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "In un pomeriggio del 1826, chissà cosa avrebbe pensato Joseph Nicéphore Niépce, se dopo aver sviluppato, dalla sua casa in Borgogna, l’eliografia Point de vue du Gras ( Vista dalla finestra a Le Gras) , avesse saputo che stava fissando nella storia il compleanno della fotografia. Quell’immagine in bianco e nero, oggi presente in tutti i libri e manuali di fotografia, é il momento zero, che ha rivoluzionato il modo di rapportarsi alle immagini. Da allora, senza lastre di peltro e bitume, per la sua riproduzione, la fotografia ha integrato ogni ambito del quotidiano: la vita privata, il lavoro, e dagli anni Trenta e Quaranta del Novecento, il mondo dell’arte come linguaggio artistico autonomo. Se la prima immagine di Niépce ha aperto le danze a due secoli di sperimentazioni fotografiche, dal 1997, a raccontarle, c’è Paris Photo 2026 . La fiera internazionale consacrée à la photographie et à l’image , con un panorama che dall’inizio del XX secolo arriva al presente."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Quest’anno, sotto il patrocinio del Ministero della Cultura francese, Paris Photo é il primo appuntamento proprio in occasione del suo 200esimo compleanno. Come sottolineano nell’intervista di Brendan Embser, le direttrici della fiera Florence Bourgeois e Anna Planas, «l’anniversario permette di non limitarsi a ripercorrere la storia della fotografia, ma di considerarne le trasformazioni». Paris Photo è un appuntamento di rito per il mondo delle immagini, che costruisce la sua identità attraverso un dialogo con il sistema dell’arte internazionale: gallerie, istituzioni, curatori e collezionismo. «Ci interessa ciò che accade quando qualcuno porta uno sguardo diverso dal nostro. Perché, Paris Photo non è soltanto una piattaforma dedicata al mercato, ma un luogo di riflessione sulla cultura visiva contemporanea». Dal 12 al 15 novembre 2026, per la sua 29esima 2026, la fiera riunisce nel Grand Palais di Parigi 244 espositori, provenienti da 38 Paesi, tra cui 197 gallerie, 47 editori e 80 nuove partecipazioni. Il suo percorso si articola su cinque settori, che mettono in dialogo numerose genealogie e campi di ricerca: Main sector, Emergence, Voices, Digital ed Editions ."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Orientarsi in una fiera strutturata come Paris Photo significa inevitabilmente compiere delle scelte. Quella che segue è una selezione di alcuni stand e progetti che colpiscono per le loro modalità di interrogare il linguaggio fotografico e il suo rapporto con il presente."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Main Sector: il corpo come immagine, l’immagine come corpo"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sotto le arcate di vetro e ferro del Grand Palais, si trova Il Main Sector, che con 150 gallerie attraversa la storia del medium. Dalle sue origini alle sperimentazioni contemporanee. Dalle prime tecniche fotografiche ottocentesche, con opere di pionieri come Daguerre, Talbot e Anna Atkins, fino alle ricerche di artisti contemporanei che ne ribaltano processi e materialità. Tra i suoi espositori, le gallerie Public Relations, Lia Rumma e Bacqueville."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La galleria Public Relations, basata tra Glasgow e New York, presenta l’artista americana Elle Pérez, con una serie che si inserisce nel percorso Elles x Paris Photo , curato da Adelaide Delgado. In dialogo con le riflessioni dell’articolo It’s Time for the W.N.B.A. to Pick Sides, pubblicato sul New York Times, 2026 , i suoi scatti esplorano il corpo femminile e il mondo del basket, tra identità, rappresentazione e trasformazione. Accanto ai corpi delle atlete sul campo da gioco, la chirurgia entra nella narrazione, portando al centro la questione dell’identità di genere in relazione al mondo delle sport.", "links": [{"text": "It’s Time for the W.N.B.A. to Pick Sides, pubblicato sul New York Times, 2026", "url": "https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/26/opinion/wnba-playoffs-culture-war.html?eafs_enabled=false"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/10.-Elle-Pérez_Public-Relations_Installation-View-Paris-Photo-2026_Ph-Linda-Motto-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Elle Pérez, Public Relations, Installation View, Paris Photo 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Dall’Italia, la galleria Lia Rumma dedica uno spazio al corpo femminile. Tra gli scatti, la documentazione della performance Rhythm 4 (1974) di Marina Abramović , l’autoritratto Seeking Martyrdom No. 1 (1995) di Shirin Neshat, e alcuni più recenti ritratti di Vanessa Beecroft."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/11.-Marina-Abramović-Rhythm-4-1974-2010-©Galleria-Lia-Rumma-site.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Marina Abramović, Rhythm 4, 1974-2010 ©Galleria Lia Rumma site, 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Da Parigi, la Galerie Bacqueville , tra i quattro fotografi selezionati, presenta l’artista franco-brasiliano Nicolas Lebeau , che espone un’opera dal carattere scultoreo. Il progetto, Silver Lining (stampa UV su plexiglas con base in acciaio), nasce da una riflessione su ciò che resta di una fabbrica, quando le macchine si fermano, i corpi degli operai scompaiono e gli edifici si trasformano in rovine. Partendo dai resti del complesso industriale Kodak di Chalon-sur-Saône, l’artista costruisce una sorta di archeologia visiva, combinando fotografie d’archivio, come immagini frammentate e recuperate online, da canali come Telegram. In Silver Lining, come in tutto il suo lavoro, lo spazio espositivo assume un ruolo fondamentale. Lebeau non si limita a presentare fotografie alle pareti, ma le trasforma in installazioni in acciaio, tra pannelli in plexiglas e superfici sospese. Giocando con le trasparenze, le immagini acquistano peso. Una presenza fisica che contrasta con la loro origine digitale. Al centro della ricerca di Lebeau ci sono spesso i corpi di chi rimane ai margini della rappresentazione. Migranti, lavoratori precari, manifestanti, giovani e persone coinvolte in conflitti o situazioni di vulnerabilità. Le fotografie diventano elementi materiali con cui ricostruire la memoria di un luogo e delle persone che lo hanno abitato."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/12.-Nicolas-Labeau-Silver-Lining_Immagine-dallartista-2026.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Nicolas Lebeau, Silver Lining, ©Nicolas Lebeau, 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Emergence, oltre la superficie: corpi, rovine e resistenza"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Il bisogno di relazionarsi allo spazio di Nicolas Lebeau, racconta di un’esigenza ambientale del corpo. Questa tensione, che porta la fotografia oltre i suoi confini bidimensionali, emerge anche dalla sezione Emergence della fiera. Parte sviluppata lungo il perimetro del primo piano del Grand Palais. Emergence propone un’esplorazione della scena artistica emergente (seppur già ben affermata), attraverso venti progetti monografici."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Da Oslo, la galleria Melk Gallery, presenta l’artista norvegese-indiano Dev Dhunsi . La sua ricerca é all’incrocio tra fotografia, tessile e installazione. Tra dimensioni scultoree e sonore. Nel processo di creazione, le sue fotografie vengono distese su tessuti, immerse nell’acqua o messe in movimento, sottraendosi alla condizione del documento statico, per diventare esperienze corporee e multisensoriali. Nello spazio le sue installazioni diventano dispositivi ambientali, che reclamano una presenza. La ricerca di Dev intreccia corpo, mito, documentazione e immaginazione, interrogando l’identità come dimensione fluida e relazionale, attraversata da dinamiche culturali, politiche e storiche."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/15.-Dev_Dhunsi_photo-Nitja__WebRes_2026-1024x683.jpg", "alt": "paris photo 2026", "caption": "Dev Dhunsi, photo Nitja, WebRes, 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La Galleria Tanit, da Beirut, presenta Randa Mirza, artista che lavora tra Beirut e Marsiglia. In occasione della fiera Mirza porta Atlal , un progetto che si confronta con la distruzione delle abitazioni nei villaggi del Libano meridionale da parte dell’esercito israeliano. In un contesto come quello di Paris Photo, il corpo di chi osserva sembra faticare a trovare un posto in queste immagini. Non ci sono più case da abitare, né spazi in cui riconoscersi. Per fotografare questi paesaggi Randa utilizza una macchina fotografica a banco ottico di grande formato. Un processo lento e meditativo, che richiama il rituale dei poeti preislamici, soliti comporre versi davanti ai resti delle abitazioni abbandonate. Nell’installazione, le fotografie delle abitazioni distrutte sono accostate a versi della tradizione araba, trascritti a mano dalla calligrafa Acyl Safa. Nella serie, le rovine non sono soltanto testimonianze di ciò che è stato abbattuto, ma spazi di lutto condiviso, in cui la perdita individuale si intreccia a una storia collettiva."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/16.-1024x768.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Randa Mirza, Exhibition View, Atlal, Galleria Tanit, 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Di un corpo che resiste e rivendica la propria presenza parla anche il lavoro di Yumna Al-Arashi, artista yemenita-egiziana-americana con base a Zurigo. Da Amsterdam, la galleria Homecoming presenta il suo lavoro Let Me In . Una serie di autoscatti di nudo, in bianco e nero, che l’artista realizza a Zurigo, accanto a sculture di donne anonime. Il corpo per Yumna è luogo di resistenza, ritualità e mito. Con il suo lavoro rivendica il diritto di autodeterminare la propria rappresentazione, confrontandosi con lo sguardo di una società che continua a definire, contenere e consumare il corpo delle donne arabe e le storie che porta con sé. «Non si tratta soltanto di mostrarsi, ma di scegliere come essere viste», racconta l’artista. Girato l’angolo, dello spazio della galleria, in fondo alla parete compare un’ultima fotografia dell’artista, accompagnata da un manifesto: La Police mutile les Lycéens . Una delle poche immagini che, all’interno della bolla della fiera, riporta l’attenzione sulle proteste che attraversano il mondo dell’istruzione, della cultura e dell’arte di questo autunno caldo."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/11/19.-Yumna-Al-Arashi-Homecoming-Installation-view-Paris-Photo-2026-1-1024x780.jpg", "alt": "paris photo 2026", "caption": "Yumna Al-Arashi, Homecoming, Installation view Paris Photo, 2026", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Fotografare il presente, prima che scompaia"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In duecento anni di storia, dall’eliografia di Niépce, alle installazioni della scena artistica emergente, a Paris Photo 2026 sembra esserci un filo che tiene insieme il suo brulichio d’immagini: il bisogno di relazionarsi a qualcosa di tangibile. Quest’anno, tra i diversi espositori, colpisce la ricerca sulla materia e sullo spazio, che porta l’immagine oltre la sua dimensione digitale. Trasformandola in una presenza fisica, che chiama in causa il corpo biologico, in rapporto ad altri corpi, alla memoria e alle tecnologie.", "links": [{"text": "Paris Photo 2026", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/mercato/paris-photo-celebra-i-200-anni-della-fotografia/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Parlando di corpi, il ritratto femminile resta una presenza importante tra le opere selezionate. Come dichiarato nel comunicato stampa, la percentuale di fotografe presenti si ferma al 38%, un dato in crescita rispetto al 20% del 2016, ma ancora lontano da una rappresentanza paritaria. article_text:
In un pomeriggio del 1826, chissà cosa avrebbe pensato Joseph Nicéphore Niépce, se dopo aver sviluppato, dalla sua casa in Borgogna, l’eliografia Point de vue du Gras ( Vista dalla finestra a Le Gras) , avesse saputo che stava fissando nella storia il compleanno della fotografia. Quell’immagine in bianco e nero, oggi presente in tutti i libri e manuali di fotografia, é il momento zero, che ha rivoluzionato il modo di rapportarsi alle immagini. Da allora, senza lastre di peltro e bitume, per la sua riproduzione, la fotografia ha integrato ogni ambito del quotidiano: la vita privata, il lavoro, e dagli anni Trenta e Quaranta del Novecento, il mondo dell’arte come linguaggio artistico autonomo. Se la prima immagine di Niépce ha aperto le danze a due secoli di sperimentazioni fotografiche, dal 1997, a raccontarle, c’è Paris Photo 2026 . La fiera internazionale consacrée à la photographie et à l’image , con un panorama che dall’inizio del XX secolo arriva al presente.

Quest’anno, sotto il patrocinio del Ministero della Cultura francese, Paris Photo é il primo appuntamento proprio in occasione del suo 200esimo compleanno. Come sottolineano nell’intervista di Brendan Embser, le direttrici della fiera Florence Bourgeois e Anna Planas, «l’anniversario permette di non limitarsi a ripercorrere la storia della fotografia, ma di considerarne le trasformazioni». Paris Photo è un appuntamento di rito per il mondo delle immagini, che costruisce la sua identità attraverso un dialogo con il sistema dell’arte internazionale: gallerie, istituzioni, curatori e collezionismo. «Ci interessa ciò che accade quando qualcuno porta uno sguardo diverso dal nostro. Perché, Paris Photo non è soltanto una piattaforma dedicata al mercato, ma un luogo di riflessione sulla cultura visiva contemporanea». Dal 12 al 15 novembre 2026, per la sua 29esima 2026, la fiera riunisce nel Grand Palais di Parigi 244 espositori, provenienti da 38 Paesi, tra cui 197 gallerie, 47 editori e 80 nuove partecipazioni. Il suo percorso si articola su cinque settori, che mettono in dialogo numerose genealogie e campi di ricerca: Main sector, Emergence, Voices, Digital ed Editions .

Orientarsi in una fiera strutturata come Paris Photo significa inevitabilmente compiere delle scelte. Quella che segue è una selezione di alcuni stand e progetti che colpiscono per le loro modalità di interrogare il linguaggio fotografico e il suo rapporto con il presente.

Main Sector: il corpo come immagine, l’immagine come corpo

Sotto le arcate di vetro e ferro del Grand Palais, si trova Il Main Sector, che con 150 gallerie attraversa la storia del medium. Dalle sue origini alle sperimentazioni contemporanee. Dalle prime tecniche fotografiche ottocentesche, con opere di pionieri come Daguerre, Talbot e Anna Atkins, fino alle ricerche di artisti contemporanei che ne ribaltano processi e materialità. Tra i suoi espositori, le gallerie Public Relations, Lia Rumma e Bacqueville.

La galleria Public Relations, basata tra Glasgow e New York, presenta l’artista americana Elle Pérez, con una serie che si inserisce nel percorso Elles x Paris Photo , curato da Adelaide Delgado. In dialogo con le riflessioni dell’articolo It’s Time for the W.N.B.A. to Pick Sides, pubblicato sul New York Times, 2026 , i suoi scatti esplorano il corpo femminile e il mondo del basket, tra identità, rappresentazione e trasformazione. Accanto ai corpi delle atlete sul campo da gioco, la chirurgia entra nella narrazione, portando al centro la questione dell’identità di genere in relazione al mondo delle sport.

Dall’Italia, la galleria Lia Rumma dedica uno spazio al corpo femminile. Tra gli scatti, la documentazione della performance Rhythm 4 (1974) di Marina Abramović , l’autoritratto Seeking Martyrdom No. 1 (1995) di Shirin Neshat, e alcuni più recenti ritratti di Vanessa Beecroft.

Da Parigi, la Galerie Bacqueville , tra i quattro fotografi selezionati, presenta l’artista franco-brasiliano Nicolas Lebeau , che espone un’opera dal carattere scultoreo. Il progetto, Silver Lining (stampa UV su plexiglas con base in acciaio), nasce da una riflessione su ciò che resta di una fabbrica, quando le macchine si fermano, i corpi degli operai scompaiono e gli edifici si trasformano in rovine. Partendo dai resti del complesso industriale Kodak di Chalon-sur-Saône, l’artista costruisce una sorta di archeologia visiva, combinando fotografie d’archivio, come immagini frammentate e recuperate online, da canali come Telegram. In Silver Lining, come in tutto il suo lavoro, lo spazio espositivo assume un ruolo fondamentale. Lebeau non si limita a presentare fotografie alle pareti, ma le trasforma in installazioni in acciaio, tra pannelli in plexiglas e superfici sospese. Giocando con le trasparenze, le immagini acquistano peso. Una presenza fisica che contrasta con la loro origine digitale. Al centro della ricerca di Lebeau ci sono spesso i corpi di chi rimane ai margini della rappresentazione. Migranti, lavoratori precari, manifestanti, giovani e persone coinvolte in conflitti o situazioni di vulnerabilità. Le fotografie diventano elementi materiali con cui ricostruire la memoria di un luogo e delle persone che lo hanno abitato.

Emergence, oltre la superficie: corpi, rovine e resistenza

Il bisogno di relazionarsi allo spazio di Nicolas Lebeau, racconta di un’esigenza ambientale del corpo. Questa tensione, che porta la fotografia oltre i suoi confini bidimensionali, emerge anche dalla sezione Emergence della fiera. Parte sviluppata lungo il perimetro del primo piano del Grand Palais. Emergence propone un’esplorazione della scena artistica emergente (seppur già ben affermata), attraverso venti progetti monografici.

Da Oslo, la galleria Melk Gallery, presenta l’artista norvegese-indiano Dev Dhunsi . La sua ricerca é all’incrocio tra fotografia, tessile e installazione. Tra dimensioni scultoree e sonore. Nel processo di creazione, le sue fotografie vengono distese su tessuti, immerse nell’acqua o messe in movimento, sottraendosi alla condizione del documento statico, per diventare esperienze corporee e multisensoriali. Nello spazio le sue installazioni diventano dispositivi ambientali, che reclamano una presenza. La ricerca di Dev intreccia corpo, mito, documentazione e immaginazione, interrogando l’identità come dimensione fluida e relazionale, attraversata da dinamiche culturali, politiche e storiche.

La Galleria Tanit, da Beirut, presenta Randa Mirza, artista che lavora tra Beirut e Marsiglia. In occasione della fiera Mirza porta Atlal , un progetto che si confronta con la distruzione delle abitazioni nei villaggi del Libano meridionale da parte dell’esercito israeliano. In un contesto come quello di Paris Photo, il corpo di chi osserva sembra faticare a trovare un posto in queste immagini. Non ci sono più case da abitare, né spazi in cui riconoscersi. Per fotografare questi paesaggi Randa utilizza una macchina fotografica a banco ottico di grande formato. Un processo lento e meditativo, che richiama il rituale dei poeti preislamici, soliti comporre versi davanti ai resti delle abitazioni abbandonate. Nell’installazione, le fotografie delle abitazioni distrutte sono accostate a versi della tradizione araba, trascritti a mano dalla calligrafa Acyl Safa. Nella serie, le rovine non sono soltanto testimonianze di ciò che è stato abbattuto, ma spazi di lutto condiviso, in cui la perdita individuale si intreccia a una storia collettiva.

Di un corpo che resiste e rivendica la propria presenza parla anche il lavoro di Yumna Al-Arashi, artista yemenita-egiziana-americana con base a Zurigo. Da Amsterdam, la galleria Homecoming presenta il suo lavoro Let Me In . Una serie di autoscatti di nudo, in bianco e nero, che l’artista realizza a Zurigo, accanto a sculture di donne anonime. Il corpo per Yumna è luogo di resistenza, ritualità e mito. Con il suo lavoro rivendica il diritto di autodeterminare la propria rappresentazione, confrontandosi con lo sguardo di una società che continua a definire, contenere e consumare il corpo delle donne arabe e le storie che porta con sé. «Non si tratta soltanto di mostrarsi, ma di scegliere come essere viste», racconta l’artista. Girato l’angolo, dello spazio della galleria, in fondo alla parete compare un’ultima fotografia dell’artista, accompagnata da un manifesto: La Police mutile les Lycéens . Una delle poche immagini che, all’interno della bolla della fiera, riporta l’attenzione sulle proteste che attraversano il mondo dell’istruzione, della cultura e dell’arte di questo autunno caldo.

Fotografare il presente, prima che scompaia

In duecento anni di storia, dall’eliografia di Niépce, alle installazioni della scena artistica emergente, a Paris Photo 2026 sembra esserci un filo che tiene insieme il suo brulichio d’immagini: il bisogno di relazionarsi a qualcosa di tangibile. Quest’anno, tra i diversi espositori, colpisce la ricerca sulla materia e sullo spazio, che porta l’immagine oltre la sua dimensione digitale. Trasformandola in una presenza fisica, che chiama in causa il corpo biologico, in rapporto ad altri corpi, alla memoria e alle tecnologie.

Parlando di corpi, il ritratto femminile resta una presenza importante tra le opere selezionate. Eppure, le donne continuano a essere più rappresentate come soggetti che come autrici. Come dichiarato nel comunicato stampa, la percentuale di fotografe presenti si ferma al 38%, un dato in crescita rispetto al 20% del 2016, ma ancora lontano da una rappresentanza paritaria. Siamo al bicentenario della fotografia, magari tra cent’anni il quadro sarà diverso.

Tornando all’affermazione delle direttrici della fiera Florence Bourgeois e Anna Planas, «ci interessa guardare ciò che accade quando qualcuno porta uno sguardo diverso dal nostro», è forse la diversità una delle possibilità che Paris Photo continua a offrire. Ogni anno la fiera si trasforma in un enorme atlante visivo, che ciascuno può attraversare e interpretare secondo la propria sensibilità. Pur restando un appuntamento di nicchia e legato al mercato, mette in circolazione una quantità e qualità di immagini, che permette di confrontarsi con sguardi multipli sullo stesso presente.

Un presente attraversato da manifestazioni, crisi climatiche e guerre, in cui anche la fotografia si trova a fare i conti con la propria fragilità. Non è un caso che la sezione Voices della fiera, curata da Francesco Zanot e Zasha Colah, sia intitolata Disparition ( La scomparsa) . Partendo dal paradosso di una fotografia nata per conservare ciò che rischia di andare perduto, la mostra si interroga sulla sua stessa instabilità, sull’autodistruzione dell’immagine e sulla possibilità di registrarne la scomparsa. Perché, in un momento storico in cui tutto è continuamente fotografato, documentato e condiviso, il rischio non è soltanto perdere le immagini, ma perdere ciò che quelle immagini cercano di raccontare.

article_text:
MYB Textiles Ltd is the last mill in the world weaving patterned Nottingham lace on traditional looms. Once there were 20 lace mills in the Irvine Valley towns of Newmilns and Darvel alone. The lace industry became the largest employer in the area for a time and flourished until the late 1970s when competition emerged from other European countries and Asia. Now the majority of their trade comes from the film, theatre, TV and entertainment industry

Margo Graham, the design director in the mill’s finishing department where the finished lace is inspected, inspects black lace in a pattern called Jane. Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

The Lace Darner, on a gable wall on Castle Street. A tribute to the skilled hand-darners who inspected and repaired lace, based on a photograph of long-serving MYB Textiles employee Janey Gray. Created by local artists Frank and Mandy Carty of Artisan ArtworksPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

MYB Textiles Ltd is the last mill in the world now weaving patterned Nottingham lace on traditional looms. Once there were 20 lace mills in the Irvine Valley towns of Newmilns and Darvel alone, employing about 2,000 peoplePhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

The looms, mostly over a century in age, date from 1913. One loom requires 10,000 spools of thread to supply its warp as it weavesPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

MYB now employs 42 people and has fought to survive in recent years. They are quietly famed for their Scottish Leno gauze weave (later known as Madras) and Nottingham lace. The former came to be called Madras because Scotland exported so much of it to India and to British colonies, because mosquitos could not get through the fine nettingPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Handloom weaving was brought to the Irvine Valley by Flemish refugees who settled in the area at the end of the 16th century. This was followed by the invention of the power loom in 1877Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Due to the antiquity of the looms, Thursday is set aside as a day for repairs and maintenance. The weavers stop the loom when a thread breaks and quickly remedy the problemPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Stocks of fine lace in the storeroom. Despite challenges, MYB Textiles has maintained high-profile collaborations with designers, institutions, performers and artists. Projects in the past have involved translating metalwork to lace, recreating archive museum textiles and collaborations with design studios such as Timorous Beasties and Eley KishimotoPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

This machine fills the brass-centred shuttles with its 400 yards of thread. One loom requires 10,000 spools of thread to supply its warp as it weavesPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Darning to replace broken or missing threads in the mill’s finishing department, where the finished lace is inspected and missing portions left in the fabric before the loom was stopped are painstakingly repairedPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Working with the V&A Design Museum in Dundee, MYB Textiles featured in the Design in Motion exhibition in 2015. They supplied material for curtains in Spielberg’s film Lincoln, and their lace has been used on the sets of Martin Scorsese’s Boardwalk Empire. Lincoln’s 12 Oscar nominations in 2013 included one for best production design, which it wonPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

A mill worker selects a pattern from a library of thousands of massive, finely punched cards. Hundreds of these lengthy, perforated cards – forerunners of computer programs – hang inside the entrance like an ancient library. There are 50,000 samples and 20,000 designs in the mill’s archivePhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Sherry Campbell, Scottish Madras designer in the finishing department. The pattern on the left is St Andrews; the one on the right is Paradiso. While they have recently sold fabric to historic houses and high-end hotels, and some to the fashion industry, the majority of MYB’s trade now comes from the film, theatre, TV and entertainment industry. Sheets of lace are used as backdrops, and scrims that can be painted with traditional patterned lace are much in demand for period drama. The company was badly affected by the US writers strike due to the effect this had on film and theatre productionPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Margo Graham, the design director in the mill’s finishing department where the finished lace is inspected, inspects black lace in a pattern called JanePhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Photographs and shuttles from the mill’s past are used for the benefit of organised heritage trail tours conducted around the millPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Cafe murals on display. Lace and madras weaving continued to flourish until the late 1970s, but companies struggled to compete with emerging European and Asian economies. This had a profound effect on the Scottish textile industryPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

Lace and Town Crest mural celebrating the town’s world-famous lace heritage on Main Street. It features a lace drape inspired by a 1936 MYB Textiles pattern called Lydia and the Newmilns crest and motto ‘Weave Truth with Trust’. Created by local artists Frank and Mandy Carty of Artisan ArtworksPhotograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

article_text:
Sponsored by 渋谷パルコ

10Fで日替わりに届く、アート、身体、映像の3企画

渋谷PARCOは、アートイベント 「SHIBUYA PARCO ART DAYS」 を11月4日から8日まで開催する。6回目となる今年は、現代美術を起点に音楽や映像、パフォーマンスなどの表現が館内各所に集まる。10F PBOX STNDでは、アートウィーク東京の一環でアーティストデュオ・MESがキュレーションするメインパーティーをはじめ、ヘラルボニーとカルチャー雑誌『BRUTUS』のコラボイベント、尹苑（イン・エン）の新作パフォーマンス、Soundwalk Collectiveによる上映が日替わりで行われる。キーヴィジュアルは、アートディレクターの永戸鉄也が手がけた。渋谷の街からカルチャーを発信してきたPARCOならではの、ジャンルの垣根を越えたラインナップが揃う。

11月7日は、尹苑が新作パフォーマンス「うまくいく」を発表する。上海出身で東京藝術大学大学院で彫刻を修めた尹苑は、社会構造が個人に内面化されることで生じる見えない束縛を、パフォーマティブ・インスタレーションによって具体化してきたアーティストだ。新作のテーマは「馬」。かつて労働や戦争を支え、近代化のなかで機械や資本の論理といった日常へと組み込まれていった「馬」を手がかりに、規則や欲望に翻弄される現代人の無意識の行動や受動的な身体を空間に描き出す。遊具やゲームを通して身近に存在する「馬」が、どのような風景へと姿を変えるのか、期待が高まる。

最終日の11月8日は、ニューヨークとベルリンを拠点とするSoundwalk Collectiveの作品『What We Leave Behind / Jean-Luc Godard Archives』が上映される。ステファン・クラズニアンスキーとシモーネ・メルリによるこのコレクティブは、サウンドと映像を軸に、特定の場所や文脈に応じた作品を生み出してきた。本作は、ゴダールの倉庫に眠っていたフィルムやメモ、本などの個人アーカイヴを撮影・採録し、映像と音響で再構成したプロジェクト。巨匠のプライベートな世界に触れられる、貴重な上映となる。

11月5日には、障害のある作家のアートを日常のプロダクトとして届けるブランド・ヘラルボニーと、カルチャー雑誌『BRUTUS』が、1日限りのイベント「あふれて、うつる。」を催す。昼の部ではヘラルボニーと契約する作家3名によるライブペインティングと音楽家のライブパフォーマンスが行われ、夜の部では昼に描かれた作品が残る会場で、DJによるレセプションパーティーが開かれる。また、1FのPOPUP SPACE「ARCADE」には11月15日までヘラルボニーのポップアップストアが出店し、作品の特徴にあわせてジャカードや刺繍、ニットなどの技法を選んだ26年秋冬コレクションが並ぶ。

MESがアートウィーク東京の夜を演出、4Fでは個展も

新井健と谷川果菜絵によるアーティストデュオ・MESは、クラブカルチャーと現代美術を行き来しながら、光や熱を用いたインスタレーションとパフォーマンスを発表しており、2027年2月にはロサンゼルス現代美術館での個展を控えている。

初日の11月4日夜、MESはDJやVJ、パフォーマーを招いたパーティー「REVOLIC -Revolution Holic/革命中毒」を開く。2022年から続くこのシリーズが、今回はアートウィーク東京のメインパーティーとなる。出演者には戸川純 avec おおくぼけいらが名を連ね、アートウィークの夜を熱く盛り上げるだろう。

4Fの 「PARCO MUSEUM TOKYO」 では、MESの個展 「レイ/RE-I」 が10月24日から11月16日まで行われる。変わり続ける渋谷の街を新たな角度からとらえなおす試みで、街にひそむ歴史のレイヤーを浮かび上がらせる映像インスタレーションと、デュレーショナルなパフォーマンスで構成される。関連企画として、9Fの「SUPER DOMMUNE」での特別番組も予定されている。さらに11月8日には、2012年に旧渋谷PARCOで個展を開いたChim↑Pom from Smappa!GroupとMESによるトークイベントが実現する。活動を広げてきたふたつの世代が、どのような言葉を交わすのか楽しみだ。

館内のギャラリーで出会う永戸鉄也、今村文、ChiMy、飯島奈美

キーヴィジュアルを制作した永戸鉄也は、広告や映像、音楽、ファッションなどの分野でアートディレクションを担い、コラージュや映像作品も手がけてきた。今回のヴィジュアルは、館内に集まった表現が呼応しあう様子をかたちにしたもので、永戸はステートメントに「街は、ひとつの完成された風景ではない」と記している。見慣れた風景を別の角度から見つめなおすという姿勢は、このイベント全体にも通じている。ZERO GATE B1Fの「NONLECTURE books/artsで」は、永戸のプロジェクト「RAREMETAL」のポップアップストア「Knowledge」もオープンする。新作アパレルやZINEレーベル「IRUBOOKS」の刊行物に加え、「コンポジシオン（未完と即興性）」をテーマにした新作コラージュが披露される。初日の11月4日には永戸本人が在廊し、微弱ノイズによる即興演奏を行う。

2Fの 「OIL by 美術手帖」 では、愛知県を拠点とする現代アーティスト・今村文の展示「花言葉」が開かれる。今村は花や植物をモチーフに、半透明のグラシン紙へ水彩のコラージュを施した作品などを制作してきた。本展は、話すたびに口から花や真珠がこぼれる魔法を描いた童話から着想を得たもので、小さな花のインスタレーションと平面作品で構成される。繊細な色彩と透明感に包まれる、可憐な展示になりそうだ。

ZERO GATE B1Fの 「NONLECTURE books/arts」 では、イラストレーターでDJのChiMyによる個展「お前へのアンチテーゼ」、8Fの 「ほぼ日曜日」 では、フードスタイリスト・飯島奈美の20年にわたる仕事を、映画『かもめ食堂』とドラマ『深夜食堂』のふたつの「食堂」を軸に振り返る 「『深夜食堂』と『かもめ食堂』展」 が開催中。 今年の「SHIBUYA PARCO ART DAYS」は、10Fで日替わりに行われるイベントと、フロアごとに異なる展示で構成される。パーティーや上演がある夜に合わせて訪れることも、昼間にギャラリーを順にめぐることもできる。イベントは11月4日から8日に集中するいっぽう、MESの個展や今村文の展示、ヘラルボニーやRAREMETALのポップアップなどは会期の前後にも開かれており、10月下旬から11月下旬まで、館内のどこかでアートに出会える。買い物や食事で通い慣れた渋谷PARCOが、いつもと違う表情を見せてくれるはずだ。

title_original: London Falling? A New Report on Three Decades of the British Art Market Finds Its Growth Trailing Rival Hubs
editorial_title_zh: 伦敦在走下坡路吗？一份关于英国艺术市场三十年的新报告显示，其增长落后于竞争对手
editorial_excerpt_zh: 该报告展示了世界第二大艺术市场如何在更大的起伏中走过。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "英国艺术市场联合会（British Art Market Federation）的报告《英国艺术市场 1996–2025》（The British Art Market 1996–2025）值此成立周年之际发布，评估了世界第二大艺术市场与其主要竞争对手美国和中国的表现相比如何。该报告由由经济学家克莱尔·麦克安德鲁（Clare McAndrew）创立的 Arts Economics 撰写，该公司也负责撰写巴塞尔艺术展/瑞银集团（Art Basel/UBS）艺术市场报告。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "好消息（对英国人来说无论如何是这样）是，按价值计算，英国是世界第二大市场，已从1996年的26亿英镑（40亿美元）增长到2025年的80亿英镑（105亿美元）。（值得注意的是，40亿美元经通胀调整后为87亿美元。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "坏消息是，近年英国市场的增长落后于其竞争对手。自2009年以来，美国市场增长了约114%，全球总销售额攀升了51%，而英国销售额仅增长了14%。英国艺术市场联合会主席安东尼·布朗（Anthony Browne）在报告中写道，该组织中的许多小型企业提到了他们所称的过度且不断增长的监管所带来的压抑效应。报告仅在因报告程序变化而导致2021年以来欧盟内部进口增长的背景下，提及了一次于2020年发生的英国脱欧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这80亿英镑的数字使英国市场成为欧洲绝对最大的市场，约占整个欧洲市场的的一半。按交易量计算，英国占全球销售额的18%，领先于法国的8%和中国的14%，但远远落后于占全球销售额44%的美国。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在30年间，英国艺术市场的历史最高点出现在2008年，当时其规模达到112亿英镑（208亿美元），随后在全球金融危机中按美元计算暴跌约57%，降至57亿英镑（89亿美元）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2025年的进口额比2015年的价值下降了45%。然而，如果审视自2000年以来的调查数据，这一数字增长了35%。报告称，虽然出口自2000年以来扩大了46%，但同比下降了15%，这可能是由于美国总统唐纳德·特朗普不断变化的关税声明所产生的“间接影响和不确定性”；毕竟，很大一部分下降归因于对美出口的减少。从稍长的时间跨度来看，随着时间推移，英国对美国贸易的依赖已有所减少，自2000年以来美国在出口中所占份额减半，进口份额也下降了几乎相同的幅度。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据该报告称，去年英国约有7610家经销商和画廊，其中约三分之一在伦敦，创造了约46亿英镑（约61亿美元）的销售额。自2003年以来，企业数量增长了三分之一。大多数是“小型或微型企业”，其中89%的企业在2025年的销售额在100万英镑（130万美元）或以下。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术博览会是这些实体商业计划中至关重要的一部分，占经销商2025年销售额的37%。他们可能会为了参加博览会而进行更多差旅；英国在2019年举办了52场艺博会，而去年举办的数量略超40场。画廊为了参与这些活动投入巨大，在2025年集体砸下了约3.15亿英镑（4.19亿美元）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "画廊的销售额呈现两极分化（头重脚轻），平均而言，最畅销的艺术家占销售额的38%，前三名创收者占59%。而且这种两极分化还在加剧；这两个数字都从2022年有所上升，前三名艺术家的收入份额从48%上升。（英国并非特例；对于全球画廊而言，前三名的份额已从51%上升到58%。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出售艺术品、古董和其他收藏品的拍卖行在英国艺术经济中占据很大比重，1170家拍卖行（在总共3500家拍卖商和拍卖室中）在2025年按价值创造了42%的销售额，总计33亿英镑（44亿美元）。这一数字在2025年增长了8%，但仍比2023年的最高点低20%。虽然售出的纯艺术拍品中有78%的估价在5000美元以下，但高达45%的销售价值是由100万美元至1000万美元价格区间的拍品贡献的。以100万美元或更高价格售出的艺术品占总价值的55%，尽管它们在交易量中所占比例不到1%。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "战后及当代艺术在拍卖市场稳居最大板块，其价值占比略低于一半。与此同时，英国在西方古代大师（Old Master）市场处于领先地位，全球份额达到38%。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据保守估计，英国艺术市场在2025年创造了15亿英镑的税收收入。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
The British Art Market Federation’s report “The British Art Market 1996–2025,” marking the anniversary of the foundation, is out now, measuring how the world’s second-largest art market has performed against its principal competitors, the United States and China. It’s authored by Arts Economics, the same firm that writes the Art Basel/UBS art market reports, founded by economist Clare McAndrew.

The good news (for the British, anyway) is that the UK is the world’s second-largest market by value, and has grown from £2.6 billion ($4 billion) in 1996 to £8 billion ($10.5 billion) in 2025. (It’s relevant to note that $4 billion, adjusted for inflation, is $8.7 billion.)

The bad news is that the UK market’s growth has lagged behind that of its competitors in recent years. While the US market has grown since 2009 by some 114% and aggregate global sales have climbed by 51%, UK sales have grown by just 14%. Many of the small businesses that are part of the organization cite what they call the stifling effects of excessive and growing regulation, writes the British Art Market Federation president Anthony Browne in the report. The report mentions Brexit, which took place in 2020, only once, in the context of a growth in imports within the EU since 2021 due to changes in reporting procedures.

That £8 billion figure made the UK’s market the largest by far in Europe, accounting for about half the entire European market. It accounted for 18% of global sales by volume, ahead of France at 8% and China at 14% but well behind the US, which constituted 44% of global sales.

Over 30 years, the UK art market’s highest-ever point was achieved in 2008, when it weighed in at £11.2 billion ($20.8 billion) before crashing down some 57% in dollar terms in the global financial crisis to £5.7 billion ($8.9 billion).

Imports in 2025 dropped by 45% from their 2015 values. When surveyed since 2000, however, that number has grown by 35%. While exports have expanded by 46% since 2000, they fell by 15% year on year, says the report, possibly due to “indirect effects and uncertainties” created by US president Donald Trump’s ever-changing announcements about tariffs; much of the decline was accounted for, after all, by the decrease in exports to the States. In the slightly longer view, the UK has been less dependent on US trade over time, with the US share of exports falling by half since 2000 and the share of imports dropping by almost the same amount.

According to the report, the UK was home to about 7,610 dealers and galleries last year, about a third of them in London, generating an estimated £4.6 billion (about $6.1 billion) in sales. The number of businesses has grown by a third since 2003. Most are “small or micro businesses,” with 89% of them notching sales of £1 million ($1.3 million) or lower in 2025.

Art fairs were a crucial part of those entities’ business plan, accounting for 37% of dealers’ 2025 sales. They may be traveling more to attend; while the UK hosted 52 fairs in 2019, it hosted just over 40 last year. Galleries dug deep to participate in these events, collectively shelling out some £315 million ($419 million) in 2025.

Galleries’ sales are top-heavy, with a top-selling artist accounting for 38% of sales on average and their top three earners accounting for 59%. And they’re only getting more top-heavy; both those numbers have ticked up from 2022, with the share of revenue from the top three artists rising from 48%. (The UK is not alone in this; for galleries globally, the top three’s share has gone from 51% to 58%.)

Auction houses that sell art, antiques and other collectibles loom large in the UK’s arts economy, with 1,170 houses (out of 3,500 auctioneers and auction rooms overall) generating 42% of sales by value in 2025, totaling £3.3 billion ($4.4 billion). That number rose 8% in 2025, but remained 20% below its high point in 2023. While 78% of fine art lots sold were valued under $5,000, fully 45% of the value of sales was accounted for by lots in the $1 million to $10 million range. Works of art sold for $1 million or up accounted for 55% of the total value, though they made up less than 1% of the transactions.

Postwar and contemporary art reigns as the largest sector in the auction market, accounting for just under half its value. At the same time, the UK leads the Old Master market, with a 38% share globally.

The UK art market generated a conservatively estimated £1.5 billion in tax revenues in 2025.

article_text:
I f Andy Burnham is looking for inspiration for his great “ council housebuilding comeback ”, he would do well to visit Croydon. There, nestled into a steeply sloping site, sheltered by a canopy of mature trees, stands a cluster of crystalline pink and brown brick towers, where generous flats look on to a landscape of allotments, playgrounds and to the rolling hills of south London beyond. Designed by Mary Duggan Architects, with Ruff Architects, it is a model of council-led housebuilding – so much so that it has also been named this year’s best building in the UK, confounding the bookies’ outsider odds.

Only once before has the RIBA Stirling prize ever been awarded to a council housing project, when Goldsmith Street in Norwich scooped the gong in 2019, for its rows of low-energy brick terraces, designed by Mikhail Riches Architects and Cathy Hawley. This year’s winner, Lion Green Road in Coulsdon, is an entirely different animal, and it puts a welcome spotlight back on housing design at a time when the government plans to pump £39bn into the sector. It is also a bittersweet vindication of Croydon council’s erstwhile housebuilding company, Brick by Brick, a bold and sadly brief experiment by the previous Labour administration, which was halted in 2020 when the council went bankrupt, seeing numerous projects cancelled.

“At a time when we urgently need to deliver more homes,” says RIBA president, Chris Williamson, “Lion Green Road shows that density can be achieved without compromising the quality of the places we create. Through a consistent specification, with subtle variation in height and orientation, it offers housing at scale without uniformity.”

Burnham’s first allocation of £10bn, announced in August, is planned to kickstart 70,000 affordable homes across the country. Yet few people in Britain welcome the prospect of new housing in their backyards, even if it’s prize-winning. The planning application for Lion Green Road, submitted in 2017, received 18 letters of support and 257 objections, mostly about the loss of parking. Now built, almost a decade later, the project demonstrates how more homes than you might imagine can be constructed on the most unpromising of sites in a sympathetic way, without sacrificing greenery, views and public access – and keeping plenty of parking, too.

“We really pushed against the suburban model of terraces dominated by cars, with little front and back gardens,” says Duggan. The original brief asked for 80 homes, arranged as she describes, but Duggan proved she could fit 157 flats, distributed between five pavilion-like towers, retaining the mature trees and bluebell woodland on the site. The result feels like it has grown out of its woodland setting, with a public route that winds its way through the site, up to a historic railway embankment at the rear, and not a perimeter fence in sight.

“Brick by Brick was an amazing client,” says Duggan, who also had a small mews project in Crystal Palace on the drawing board for the council’s housebuilder, before the plug was pulled. “It was a refreshing change from how private developers think about affordable housing. Here, they weren’t talking about the land as a commodity, but as a genuinely public asset.”

The council cared about the interior spaces, too. Thanks to the “pinwheel” plan of the blocks, with flats radiating outwards from a central lift core, each home is dual aspect, maximising natural light, cross-ventilation and views. The flats all enjoy an inset loggia balcony, with a bulge at the base of the balustrades to accommodate plant pots, while cuts in the form (to preserve historic views) create some with larger roof terraces. In the interests of efficiency, the five towers all have the same star-shaped plan, but each is subtly rotated to reduce direct overlooking between neighbouring homes, enabling the buildings to stand close together without sacrificing privacy. Half of the flats are private rental, in two towers, while half are affordable, in three blocks retained by the council, rented at local housing allowance rates. Unlike the Norwich project, this is not true social housing.

The RIBA judges describe the project as a “new kind of garden neighbourhood”. The space between the blocks feels consciously planned, rather than a leftover afterthought, designed with landscape architecture practice Planit to include a sensory garden, allotment plots and play areas. Walking around the development’s zig-zagging slopes and stepped pathways gives the feeling of exploring a bucolic hill town. Little bug hotels in the same faceted star-shaped form as the towers are a delightful touch; even the insects get a dignified dwelling.

Duggan says the project “expands the idea of the threshold”, and the arrival feels more welcoming than most. The entrance of each block is framed by a paved terrace, with seating and planting, while all have generous lobbies, no matter the tenure. It’s a far cry from the “poor door” apartheid of so much developer-built housing, where private owners get the hotel concierge treatment, while affordable tenants enter around the back by the bins. It all oozes quality on a budget, down to the choice of three dusty colours of brick, some projecting to create a textured, tweedy finish. The quality belies the tight construction budget of £2,500/sq metre – making it the cheapest project on the shortlist by far. Other Stirling Prize contenders this year included two exquisitely built projects for well-heeled Cambridge colleges, a large private house in Essex, an arts centre in Hertford, and an £825m office block in Paddington.

If there is a cloud hanging over Croydon’s triumph, it is the fate of Brick by Brick. It was established in 2015, as a wholly council-owned company, because the conventional development model was failing to deliver enough affordable homes . The idea was that Croydon would use its own land, often small leftover sites, and borrow against its own resources, to build a mix of private and affordable housing, while turning a profit for the public purse. But the sites often proved to be trickier than expected, adding additional costs, while the financial forecasts were overly optimistic, with Brexit and Covid introducing huge delays. Housing experts attribute its collapse to poor financial structuring, governance and risk management, rather than a failure in development expertise or quality of delivery.

Nonetheless, Brick by Brick built 751 homes, over half of which are affordable, of a design quality higher than most standard developer fare. With renewed housing cash from central government, might there be a chance for some of the halted schemes to be resurrected, and more of the imagination and innovation of Lion Green Road spread across the borough and beyond?

article_text:
Filme tem estreia prevista para 28 de julho de 2028.

Um dos nomes mais badalados em Hollywood atualmente, Connor Storrie se juntou ao MCU. Ele fará parte do elenco de “ Motoqueiro Fantasma “, estrelado por Ryan Gosling. Segundo o THR , ele deve interpretar um vilão.

Storrie tornou-se um dos grandes destaques de 2025 ao estrelar a série romântica “Rivalidade Ardente” junto a Hudson Williams, com uma segunda temporada já em produção. Desde então, ele já apresentou o humorístico “Saturday Night Live” e gravou uma participação em “A Redoma de Vidro”, dirigido por Sarah Polley. Nas telonas, “Motoqueiro Fantasma” será seu primeiro grande papel de destaque.

Não se sabe ainda qual vilão Storrie interpretaria. O herói Johnny Blaze não tem um vilão principal em suas histórias, tendo um panteão de antagonistas demoníacos em vez disso. Nos filmes produzidos pela Sony e estrelados por Nicolas Cage, os vilões incluíam Mefisto e seu filho, Coração Negro — Mefisto, no entanto, já apareceu no MCU interpretado por Sacha Baron Cohen na série “Coração de Ferro”.

O personagem Johnny Blaze foi criado pelo roteirista Gary Friedrich e pelo artista Mike Ploog, surgindo pela primeira vez na edição nº 5 de “Marvel Spotlight”, em 1972. Um ano depois, o personagem ganhou sua própria série. Blaze é um motociclista dublê que, após um pacto com o diabo, une-se a um demônio chamado Zarathos. Ele se transforma em um espírito de vingança com cabeça de caveira em chamas, que pilota uma motocicleta flamejante.

Shawn Levy dirige o novo filme após o sucesso de “Deadpool e Wolverine” e o término da produção de “Star Wars: Starfighter”, no qual Gosling também estrela. O roteiro fica a cargo de Jonathan Tropper.

“Motoqueiro Fantasma” tem estreia prevista para 28 de julho de 2028.

article_text:
Tarek Atoui is a sound artist and composer whose installations change how we experience sound, not only through our ears but through our whole bodies. For the Hyundai Commission, Atoui transforms the Turbine Hall into a vast sonic landscape, bringing ancient families of instruments into dialogue with electronic technologies. Inspired by the unique acoustic and spatial properties of the Turbine Hall, the commission builds on decades of Atoui’s collaboration with instrument-makers, researchers, engineers and musicians.

Wind is channelled through a suspended network of bamboo pipes, playing shengs, mouth organs from China and Southeast Asia, in chorus. Korean drums struck by mechanised mallets are dispersed throughout the space alongside Uzbek karnai horns and 3D-printed horns made from sugar resin and bamboo dust. Textiles up to 30 metres long oscillate in response to wind currents of the Turbine Hall. Each material generates and transmits sound in a different way. Microphones embedded within the installation sample the sounds of the instruments and the Turbine Hall itself. Custom software developed by the artist reworks these sounds and plays them back into the space alongside the instruments, so the soundscape is always changing and no two visits are the same.

Atoui invites visitors to wander at their own pace, sit or lie on stones placed along the ground, and experience them vibrate with sound. Building on childhood memories of time spent under vine-covered canopies and sheltered courtyards across the Mediterranean, Atoui imagines the Turbine Hall as a space of gathering and exchange.

Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui is in partnership with Hyundai Motor. Supported by the Tarek Atoui Supporters Circle and Tate Americas Foundation.

Performances

The installation regularly transforms into a space for performance over the course of the commission. Atoui has invited a network of musicians across multiple genres to plug into the installation as a sound system and compose, improvise and play:

Sessions 1 and 2: 16 and 17 October: Tarek Atoui, Emptyset, Mazen Kerbaj, Kenichi Iwasa and Aya Metwalli

Session 3: 13 November: Bendik Giske, Valentina Magaletti

Session 4: 27 November: Nkisi, Mhamad Safa

Session 5: 11 December: Elvin Brandhi, Gwilly Edmondez, Theodora Laird, Phil Minton, Elaine Mitchener, Maggie Nicols, Dylan Nyoukis, Saadet Türköz

Session 6: 15 January: Shakeeb Abu Hamdan, Li-Chin Li, Pike

Session 7: 19 February: Performance to be announced

Session 8: 19 March: Performance to be announced

Session 9: 2 April: Performance to be announced

The performances are free with a ticket. See the main Live Programme page for more information and links to book.

Exhibition guide

Learn more about this installation with our exhibition guide .

Accessibility

All Tate Modern entrances are step-free. You can enter via the Turbine Hall and into the Natalie Bell Building on Holland Street, or into the Blavatnik Building on Sumner street.

There are lifts to every floor of the Blavatnik and Natalie Bell buildings. Alternatively you can take the stairs.

Fully accessible toilets are located on every floor on the concourses.

A quiet room is available to use in the Natalie Bell Building on Level 4.

Ear defenders can be borrowed from the Ticket desks.

title_original: Sir Patrick Stewart, de X-Men e Star Trek: A Nova Geração, morre aos 86 anos

article_text:
Ator travava uma longa batalha contra o mal de Alzheimer e demência por corpos de Lewy.

Sir Patrick Stewart , conhecido por seu trabalho nos filmes de “ X-Men ” e na série “ Star Trek: A Nova Geração “, morreu nesta quarta-feira (29) aos 86 anos em Los Angeles por decorrências do mal de Alzheimer e da demência por corpos de Lewy (via THR ).

A informação já foi confirmada por suas redes oficiais , com sua empresária, Kelly Bush Novak, fazendo o anúncio inicial:

“Anunciamos, com profundo pesar, o falecimento de Sir Patrick Stewart, ocorrido ontem em sua residência em Los Angeles, sob os cuidados carinhosos de sua amada esposa, Sunny, após uma breve e comovente jornada enfrentando a doença de Alzheimer e a demência com corpos de Lewy. Ele esteve envolto pelo abraço afetuoso de familiares e amigos, cercado por música ao vivo, orações, lágrimas, risadas e aquele tipo de emoção profunda que só ele era capaz de despertar, após uma vida inteira de dedicação a todos nós. Guardaremos para sempre a imagem de serenidade e reflexão em seu rosto — uma lembrança perene de sua graça inabalável.”

Os papéis de maior destaque de Stewart nas telas vieram entre as décadas de 1980 e 2000. Já com vasta experiência e repertório no teatro britânico, Stewart assumiu o papel do capitão Jean-Luc Picard em “Star Trek: A Nova Geração”, que manteve por sete temporadas, quatro filmes e uma série revival, “Star Trek: Picard”.

Outro papel emblemático da carreira de Stewart é o de Charles Xavier, o Professor X, nos filmes da saga “X-Men”. Ele foi o primeiro intérprete do personagem no filme homônimo do ano 2000, mantendo o papel por mais seis filmes até “Logan”, o último produzido pela Fox. Já sob comando da Marvel nos cinemas, Xavier retornou em “Doutor Estranho no Multiverso da Loucura”, com Stewart fazendo sua despedida do papel em “Vingadores: Doutor Destino” em dezembro deste ano. A partir de então, Xavier será vivido por Christopher Abbott .

Além dos cinemas e da televisão, Stewart era também reconhecido como ícone do teatro britânico e um dos maiores intérpretes de Shakespeare nas últimas décadas, tendo conquistado dois Prêmios Olivier e sendo indicado a um Tony Award. Entre as demais conquistas está um Grammy e indicações ao Emmy, ao SAG Award e ao Globo de Ouro.

Em 2001, Stewart foi condecorado com a Ordem do Império Britânico (OBE) pela Rainha Elizabeth II e, posteriormente, nomeado Cavaleiro do Império Britânico em 2010, recebendo oficialmente o título de Sir.

Sir Patrick Stewart deixa a esposa, Sunny Ozell, e os filhos Daniel e Sophie, além de uma legião de fãs e admiradores.

title_original: Ken Russell’s ‘The Devils’ Feels More Relevant Than It Did 55 Years Ago. That’s Because It’s About a World Gone Mad
editorial_title_zh: 肯·拉塞尔的《恶魔》比55年前更具现实意义。那是因为它讲述了一个陷入疯狂的世界
editorial_excerpt_zh: 我是肯·拉塞尔的狂热粉丝，但我一直认为《恶魔》是一部越轨的新奇之作：一场将极度亵渎与极度恐怖集于一身的感官演练。毫无疑问：它两者兼具。然而我从未认为它超出此范畴。（对我而言，这就够了。）…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "我是肯·拉塞尔的狂热粉丝，但我一直认为《恶魔》是一部越轨的新奇之作：一场将极度亵渎与极度恐怖集于一身的感官演练。毫无疑问：它两者兼具。然而我从未认为它超出此范畴。（对我而言，这就够了。）", "links": [{"text": "Ken Russell", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ken-russell/"}, {"text": "The Devils", "url": "https://variety.com/t/the-devils/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当这部电影于1971年上映时，它正处于极端电影浪潮的前沿——这股浪潮如同一头被评为限制级的野兽，从反文化的泥沼中崛起。斯坦利·库布里克的《发条橙》和萨姆·佩金帕的《稻草狗》均于1971年上映。约翰·沃特斯当时已经开始发明朋克及其他肮脏的事物——他那部革命性的午夜电影《粉红火烈鸟》于1972年问世，同年也迎来了以《最后一座房子》为开端的剥削恐怖片黎明。在当时，这些电影是对一切体面与尊贵之物的公然唾弃。它们低俗、暴力而危险。仅仅去看其中一部，都可能被视作一种反社会行为。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/0130_051.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "数字流媒体体育转播权", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "亚特兰大老鹰队与亚马逊 Prime Video 达成流媒体合作", "links": [{"text": "Atlanta Hawks Strike Streaming Alliance With Amazon's Prime Video", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/atlanta-hawks-streaming-rights-amazon-prime-video-1236917019/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Carrie-Prime-Video.png?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "饰卡莉·怀特的萨默·H·豪厄尔", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "亚马逊首席执行官称 Prime Video 已实现盈利且每年产生“数百亿美元”收入；第三季度内容支出增长7%至59亿美元", "links": [{"text": "Amazon CEO Says Prime Video Is Profitable and Generates 'Tens of Billions of Dollars' Annually; Content Spending Grew 7% in Q3 to $5.9 Billion", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/prime-video-profitable-content-spending-q3-amazon-ceo-1236935186/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "要说现在的文化已经赶上了它们，并不意味着这些电影本身比过去不那么危险了。老实说，看到由华纳兄弟旗下名为 Warner Bros. Clockwork 的部门进行全方位修复并重新上映的《恶魔》如今正在吸引大批观众，我感到非常震惊。在其上映的首个周末，它在350家影院放映，斩获了近200万美元票房。这并不是半个世纪前那些一度引发丑闻的艺术电影通常会发生的事情。当这部经过修复且未经删剪的新版《恶魔》在戛纳首映时，我原以为它最终只会登陆少数几家影院，本质上变成一部流媒体发行作品。我从未想象过观众会蜂拥而至。但当我两周前（在一家座无虚席的影院里）观看它时，我能感受到那种兴奋感以及现实意义。超乎我的想象，《恶魔》是一部现在能够直击我们这个时代的电影。", "links": [{"text": "premiered at Cannes", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/blood-blasphemy-and-boning-ken-russells-the-devils-turns-55-at-cannes-1236751045/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种现实意义首先源于它是一部极其出色的电影（远超我的想象），这一事实曾被所有围绕它的恶劣争议所掩盖。影片以17th世纪的法国为背景，围绕一位由奥利弗·里德以精湛演技饰演的罗马天主教神父展开，他过着放荡不羁的生活。他与年轻女性发生性关系并以此自我辩解：在他看来，归根结底就是——如果感觉良好，上帝一定这样规定了。《恶魔》的风格宛如一则终极版失落天主教童话，这也是它当年惹上大麻烦的部分原因。多年来，这部电影一直遭受审查、删剪和禁映。但所有这一切，对于像我们这样可以被称为“客厅起义时代”的时期来说，如今不过是极具吸引力的诱饵。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从其非凡的开场序列——一场配以《阿维尼ョン舞曲》反常轻快节奏、带有半裸变装国王路易十三（格雷厄姆·阿米蒂奇饰）的巴洛克式舞台演出开始，《恶魔》便以其对颓废风貌的成熟唤起吸引着观众。影片并非一定要为里德饰演的乌尔班·格朗迪埃神父的不良行为辩护，他被刻画成一个冷酷的花花公子；当他得知情妇怀孕时，便冷酷无情地将她甩掉。然而，奥利弗·里德那光芒四射的明星表演让我们站在了这位拥有极大缺陷的反英雄一边，这也是影片构思的一部分。里德带着奥利弗式的恶棍轻声邪笑，饰演了一个既道德又非道德的人。他的格朗迪埃深陷恶习，但其对自由的信念绝非虚伪；他领导了一场运动，以保持卢丹这座防御城市保持独立。正是这一点让他招惹了国王路易以及其更加阴险狡诈的独裁心腹黎塞留枢机主教（克里斯托弗·洛格饰）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了镇压格朗迪埃，国王的代表们密谋通过其堕落的证据来摧毁他。这导火索是，以驼背修道院院长珍妮·德·安热修女（瓦妮莎·雷德格雷夫饰）为首的乌尔苏拉修道院修女们对格朗迪埃着迷不已——这位她们所有人都暗自渴望的摇滚巨星般的神父。一场阴谋随即展开，暗示整个修道院已被格朗迪埃迷住。修女们是被恶魔附身了吗？并没有。但她们希望自己被附身（在精神上，她们渴望加入反文化的狂欢），而针对格朗迪埃的阴谋为她们提供了借口，这正是影片轰动效应设计的一部分。", "links": [{"text": "Vanessa Redgrave", "url": "https://variety.com/t/vanessa-redgrave/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《恶魔》的疯狂之处在于，它将政治压迫转化为了一场由狂乱的色情噩梦与恐怖秀交织出的政治戏剧。它借此阐明了这样一个观点：法西斯主义的领导者为了达到目的，会不择手段。他们会制造混乱并利用混乱。这种寓言般的力量以一种独特而惊人的方式，直击我们当下所处的政治、社会和精神混乱。随着电影进入其疯狂的核心段落——修女们褪去长袍（她们剃光的头让人联想到出庭受审的曼森家族女孩们），变得“着魔”——你能感受到拉塞尔作为一个电影人的病态天才，感受到他那种让整部电影氛围彻底失控的手法。《恶魔》向我们展示的是一个陷入疯狂的世界。但这部电影带来的全新震撼在于，这个世界如今让人不安地感觉就像是我们自己的世界。今天观看《恶魔》，不仅是为了沉迷于“亵渎”或禁忌的感官盛宴，更是为了审视那个中心已然崩塌的可怕奇观。", "translated": true}]

No doubt: It’s both those things. Yet I didn’t think it was anything more than that. (For me, that was enough.)", "links": [{"text": "Ken Russell", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ken-russell/"}, {"text": "The Devils", "url": "https://variety.com/t/the-devils/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "When the film came out, in 1971, it was at the cutting edge of a movement of extreme cinema that was rising up, like an X-rated beast, out of the swamp of the counterculture. Stanley Kubrick’s “A Clockwork Orange” and Sam Peckinpah’s “Straw Dogs” were both released in 1971. article_text:
I’m an ardent fan of Ken Russell , yet I always considered “ The Devils ” to be a transgressive novelty: a voluptuous exercise in extreme blasphemy and extreme horror. No doubt: It’s both those things. Yet I didn’t think it was anything more than that. (For me, that was enough.)

When the film came out, in 1971, it was at the cutting edge of a movement of extreme cinema that was rising up, like an X-rated beast, out of the swamp of the counterculture. Stanley Kubrick’s “A Clockwork Orange” and Sam Peckinpah’s “Straw Dogs” were both released in 1971. John Waters was already at work inventing punk and other filthy things — his revolutionary midnight movie “Pink Flamingos” would come out in 1972, the year that would also bring the dawn of the slasher film, with “The Last House on the Left.” At the time, these were movies that spat in the face of eveything decent and respectable. They were skeevy and violent and dangerous. Just going to see one of them could feel like an antisocial act.

Related Stories

Amazon CEO Says Prime Video Is Profitable and Generates 'Tens of Billions of Dollars' Annually; Content Spending Grew 7% in Q3 to $5.9 Billion

To say that the culture has now caught up with them doesn’t mean that the films themselves are any less dangerous than they were. I was honestly shocked to see that “The Devils,” which has been given a full-scale restoration and re-release by a division of Warner Bros. called Warner Bros. Clockwork, is a movie that’s now drawing crowds. In its opening weekend, it played in 350 theaters and made nearly $2 million. That isn’t the sort of thing that tends to happen with once-scandalous art films from half a century ago. When this restored — and newly uncut — version of “The Devils” premiered at Cannes , I figured it would end up playing at a few theaters and, in essence, become a streaming release. I never imagined that crowds would be flocking to it. But when I saw it two weekends ago (in a packed theater), I could feel the excitement, and the relevance. More than I would ever have guessed, “The Devils” is a movie that now speaks to our time.

The relevance begins with the fact that it’s a fantastic film (much more so than I thought), something that wound up being obscured by all the nasty controversies that engulfed it. The movie is set in 17th-century France and centers on a Roman Catholic priest, played with searing brilliance by Oliver Reed, who is living the life of a libertine. He sleeps with young women and justifies it because in his mind it comes down to: If it feels good, God must have decreed it. “The Devils” plays like the ultimate lapsed-Catholic fairy tale, and that’s part of what got it in hot water at the time. Over the years, the film has been censored, butchered, and banned. But all of that is now just catnip to an era like ours, which might be called the Age of Armchair Insurrection.

From its extraordinary opening sequence, a baroque stage enactment of The Birth of Venus set to the perverse jauntiness of “Bourrée d’Avignon,” featuring King Louis XIII (Graham Armitage) in semi-nude drag, “The Devils” lures the audience with its ripe evocation of decadence. The film doesn’t necessarily justify the bad behavior of Reed’s Father Urbain Grandier, who is shown to be a callous playboy; when he learns that his mistress is pregnant, he cuts her loose with cold abandon. Yet it’s part of the film’s design that Oliver Reed’s scintillating star performance puts us on the side of this maximally flawed antihero. Reed, with his Olivier-as-wicked-knave soft-voiced leer, is playing both a moral and an immoral man. His Grandier is steeped in vice, yet his belief in freedom is no sham; he leads a crusade to keep the fortified city of Loudun an independent place. And that’s what gets him into trouble with King Louis and his even more scheming tyrannical henchman, Cardinal Richelieu (Christopher Logue).

To clamp down on Grandier, the king’s representatives hatch a plan to destroy him through evidence of his depravity. This keys off the fact that the nuns of the Ursuline convent, led by the hunchbacked abbess Sister Jeanne des Anges ( Vanessa Redgrave ), are obsessed with Grandier, the rock-star priest they all secretly desire. A plot is launched to suggest that the entire convent has been bewitched by Grandier. Are the nuns possessed by devils? No. But it’s part of the film’s sensationalist design that they wish they were (in spirit, they want to join the orgy of the counterculture), and the plot against Grandier gives them the excuse.

The insanity of “The Devils” is that it turns political oppression into the political theater of a frenzied erotic-nightmare horror show. It does this to illustrate the following idea: that the leaders of fascism will resort to any means necessary to achieve their ends. They will create chaos and use it. And there’s an allegorical power to that that speaks to the chaos of our moment — political, social, spiritual — in a singular and surprising way. As the film moves into its demented centerpiece, where the nuns, casting off their robes (their shaved heads are redolent of the Manson girls in court), become “possessed,” you feel Russell’s sick genius as a film- maker, his way of creating a vibe of the entire movie spinning out of control. What “The Devils” shows us is a world gone mad. But the film’s fresh shock is that this world now feels disturbingly like our own. To see “The Devils” today isn’t just to revel in “blasphemy” or the voluptuous excess of the forbidden. It’s to gaze upon the scary spectacle of the center no longer holding.
