article_text:
Odysseus and his intrepid crew sailed through Comcast ’s latest quarter as Universal surpassed $5 billion at the global box office, led by the The Odyssey , now Universal’s highest-grossing film of all time.

The Christopher Nolan smash based on Homer’s epic has grossed nearly $1.9 billion worldwide since its July opening and set all sorts of records for the director and the studio with $625 million domestically and $1.16 million of international box office.

Related Stories

‘The Odyssey’ Sails Past Another Milestone, Crosses $1 Billion At International Box Office

‘The Odyssey’ Slays ‘Jurassic World’ To Become Universal’s Highest-Grossing Movie Ever At Global Box Office With $1.68 Billion

Theatrical revenue surged 77% to $1.13 billion for the third quarter.

Peacock delivered its second consecutive profitable quarter with $261 million of adjusted EBITDA on $1.8 billion in revenue, driven by strong growth in distribution. Subscribers of 48 million held steady from Q2.

Watch on Deadline

Comcast reported consolidated pro forma revenue of about $29.3 billion for the quarter ended in September and adjusted EBITDA, also pro forma, of $9.1 billion, both about flat from the year earlier. The proforma numbers reflect the spinoff of Versant early this year, housing the former NBCU cable networks (except Bravo) and some digital assets.

The stock, which has taken a hit (down over 20% year to date) is having a nice premarket run on the numbers, up 2.3%.

In another major restructuring, Comcast plans to spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into a standalone company, separate from Comcast’s core Connectivity & Platforms business.

The NBCUniversal side will be run by Comcast’s current co-CEO Mike Cavanagh. Comcast’s former CFO Michael Angelakis will become CEO of Comcast after the separation and is working as a strategic advisor until then. Wall Street has been enthusiastic about the separation, which is designed to unlock the value of each group of assets and is likely to generate M&A interest.

Execs said today they are “making meaningful progress on the separation of NBCUniversal and Sky, which remains on track to create two independent companies with the financial strength and flexibility to pursue their respective growth strategies.”

Separately last summer, Sky inked a £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) deal to acquire ITV‘s television network operations , a major shakeup in the UK media landscape.

Theme parks continued to see softness. Last quarter, execs cited higher travel prices and weaker consumer sentiment. The ongoing U.S.-Iran war has squeezed oil markets and inflated the price of gasoline and jet fuel, making travel more expensive and increasing other costs for consumers and businesses. Higher interest rates are also squeezing budgets.

Profit at parks fell 17% to $780 million on revenue down 4.4% to $2.6 billion.

At Connectivity, residential broadband net losses continue amid aggressive fiber and fixed wireless access competition. Investors are laser focused on whether the company can stabilize performance there without pressuring profitability given the fierce competition.

Total domestic broadband residential customer net losses were 144,000; total domestic wireless line net additions were 368,000 and total domestic video customer net losses were 274,000.

The stock took a hit last month when Comcast CFO Jason Armstrong called certain promotional price points then in the broadband market “irrational” (presumably referring primarily to AT&T’s, although a competitor wasn’t explicitly named),” says MoffettNathanson in a September report titled U.S. Broadband Pricing: Back From The Brink? – positing the idea that prices have started rising.

Wireless and Business Services, led by Enterprise, the bright spots.

Execs said today that near-term connectivity results “reflect the investments we’re making to navigate an increasingly dynamic environment. We’re encouraged by improving customer satisfaction, strong conversion of free wireless lines to paid relationships, growing adoption of premium wireless plans across our 10.6 million total wireless lines and healthy growth in Business Services, led by Enterprise.”

More to come

article_text:
Erik von Detten, the former Disney star known for his roles in “The Princess Diaries” and “Brink!” is facing a lawsuit alleging elder abuse and fraud after an elderly couple claimed he persuaded them to invest more than $2 million of their retirement savings in significantly overpriced gold coins.

The lawsuit, filed in California in May, names von Detten, 44, and his employer, precious metals company Rosland Capital, as defendants. Sheila Greenberg, 85, and her husband, Norman Greenberg, 97, allege they lost approximately $900,000 after purchasing gold coins through the company.

Related Stories

Rosland Capital has ceased operations and declared bankruptcy in July, listing some $64 million in liabilities and just $500,000 in assets. According to filings in the bankruptcy case, the company has faced scrutiny from the New York Attorney General’s Office and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The creditors’ committee is seeking to subpoena Von Detten as it investigates the failure of the company, saying it appears he “played an instrumental part in the Debtor’s business and its financial collapse.”

“The Greenbergs’ story is not unique,” the creditors’ committee alleges. “It is one of hundreds. Creditors, including the other Committee members, have described remarkably similar experiences: trust cultivated, expertise professed, reliance encouraged, and substantial savings ultimately lost with zero information about where their money has gone.”

Rosland advertised on Fox News and Newsmax with spots starring actor William Devane, who pitched gold coins as a hedge against inflation and other sources of instability. Retirees were encouraged to convert their IRAs into gold-backed funds, and were offered “a free safe to store your gold.”

According to their lawsuit, the Greenbergs contacted Rosland Capital in 2020 after seeing an ad on TV. They were connected with von Detten, who had joined the company in 2018 after largely stepping away from acting.

The Greenbergs say they told von Detten they had limited knowledge of the gold market but approximately $2 million available in retirement savings. They allege that von Detten presented himself as an experienced adviser and encouraged them to purchase Lady Liberty gold coins as an investment.

Von Detten did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Rosland reported $151 million in revenues in 2021. But according to the company’s first-day filing in bankruptcy court, the company suffered “excessive cash outflows” and racked up net losses of $24 million from 2022-25. The rising cost of gold also put a strain on the company’s business, as it was unable to keep up with customer demand, resulting in a months-long backlog in orders.

“During this interval, the price of gold usually increased dramatically such that Debtor ended up paying more for the gold product than the customer paid Debtor for that product,” the company’s accountants reported. “This situation was not sustainable and the Debtor lost money rapidly.”

Sales reps were paid 15%-35% of the profit on each order, regardless of whether that order was later refunded. When the company ceased operations, there were about 470 messages and voicemails either demanding refunds or demanding delivery of gold products, according to the first-day motion.

The creditors’ committee, however, does not appear to believe that the business simply failed due to deteriorating market conditions.

“The Committee believes the facts point to something far more troubling: a business that preyed on a vulnerable population, stole customer money while its ability to perform was collapsing, lied to its own customers about what their money would be used for, and ultimately left creditors to ask whether those funds were misused, diverted, transferred to insiders or affiliates, or simply consumed to keep the scheme alive,” the committee’s attorneys wrote.

Von Detten was a familiar face in Disney productions throughout he late 1990s and early 2000s. He starred as the title character in the 1998 Disney original movie “Brink!” and played Josh Bryant, the love interest of Anne Hathaway’s Mia Thermopolis, in 2001’s “The Princess Diaries.”

He also voiced Sid Phillips, the toy-destroying neighbor in “Toy Story” and Erwin Lawson in Disney’s animated series “Recess.” His other credits include “Escape to Witch Mountain,” “So Weird” and “Complete Savages.”

Von Detten largely retired from acting around 2010, later transitioning into sales and financial services. He briefly reprised his role as Sid in “Toy Story 4.”

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "每个人都有自己的天鹅之歌，无论他们自己是否意识得到。但对亚历克斯·考克斯而言，他的最新电影《死魂灵》——一部大致根据尼古拉·果戈理1842年小说改编的黑色喜剧西部片——被宣传为他的最后一部电影。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果这真的是他的最后一部电影，这位风格极其独立的英国电影人可以回首一段了不起的非凡历程。他凭借1984年的朋克经典《栖息地管理员》崭露头角，随后执导了加里·奥德曼在《席德与南希》中饰演席德·维瑟斯的影片。他在1987年执导了由埃德·哈里斯主演的政治“西部片”《随走者》（Walker）——接着在1988年至1994年间，作为BBC二台《电影大观》（Moviedrome）的初代主持人，向观众引介了邪典电影与被忽视的佳作，这基本上比YouTube诞生早了几十年，干的就是电影书呆子在YouTube上做的事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他在1990年代前往墨西哥拍片，包括出色的《高速巡警》（Highway Patrolman），随后回到他的家乡利物浦拍摄了《三个生意人》（Three Businessmen）与《复仇者的悲剧》（The Revengers Tragedy）。回到美国后，考克斯制作了《搜索者2.0》（Searchers 2.0，对经典西部片的现代翻新）、《栖息地辣妹》（Repo Chick，续集）以及科幻喜剧《银河英雄比尔》（Bill the Galactic Hero）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《死魂灵》中，考克斯还亲自出演了斯特林德勒（Strindler）——还是说叫施温德勒（Swindler，意为骗子）？——一个在美国西部流浪的神秘浪子，他提出要买下死去墨西哥劳工的名字，随后却与法外之徒、腐败官员以及自己那些日益离奇的谎言纠缠在一起。演员阵容中还包括爱德华·图多-波尔（Edward Tudor-Pole）——朋克乐队主唱、演员兼前《水晶迷宫》（Crystal Maze）主持人——所以至少身边还会有人提醒考克斯，他的时间不多了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那么，考克斯这是要学昆汀吗？请在11月4日周三中午之前在下方发布你的问题，我们将把他的最佳回答刊登在我们的读者专访系列中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "电影", "links": [{"text": "Film", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/film"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "电影与音乐读者专访", "links": [{"text": "Film & Music reader interview", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/culture/series/the-reader-interview"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "文学改编电影", "links": [{"text": "Film adaptations", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/film/film-adaptations"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "尼古拉·果戈理", "links": [{"text": "Nikolai Gogol", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/books/nikolai-gogol"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "互动专栏", "links": [{"text": "callout", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/tone/callout"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
Everybody has their swansong, whether they know it or not. But for Alex Cox, his latest film Dead Souls – a darkly comic western loosely based on Nikolai Gogol’s 1842 novel – is billed as his final film.

If it really is his last film, the fiercely independent British film-maker can look back on a helluva run. He broke through with 1984 punk classic Repo Man, then went on to direct Gary Oldman as Sid Vicious in Sid and Nancy. He made the political “western” Walker in 1987, starring Ed Harris – then from 1988 to 1994 introduced viewers to cult and overlooked films as the original presenter of BBC Two’s Moviedrome, essentially doing film nerd YouTube decades before YouTube existed.

He ended up making films in Mexico in the 1990s, including the brilliant Highway Patrolman, then returned to his home town of Liverpool for Three Businessmen and The Revengers Tragedy. Back in the US Cox made Searchers 2.0 (an update of the classic western), Repo Chick (a sequel) and sci-fi comedy Bill the Galactic Hero.

In Dead Souls, Cox also stars as Strindler – or is it Swindler? – a mysterious drifter roaming the American west offering to buy the names of dead Mexican labourers, before becoming tangled up with outlaws, crooked officials and his own increasingly tall tales. The cast also includes Edward Tudor-Pole – punk frontman, actor and former Crystal Maze host – so at least there’ll be someone around to tell Cox when his time is running out.

So is Cox about to do a Tarantino? Post your questions below by midday on Wednesday 4 November, and we’ll print his best answers as part of our Readers’ Interview series.

Ahead of planned protests Saturday, the Fondation Louis Vuitton plans to close its doors out of precaution, ARTnews has learned. New anti-government protests about social and economic inequalities are expected in Paris and other European cities this weekend, sparking rumors that Art Basel may also have to close early as a result. Reporter Julie Brener Davich posted on Instagram that the fair stated that “at this stage we have nothing to share. We remain in close contact with the Paris Police Prefecture and all relevant authorities and will communicate any decision as soon as practicable.” ARTnews has contacted Art Basel for comment. Meanwhile, the Instagram account Documentations Art has called on readers to “take the Grand Palais,” where Art Basel is held, in a form of protest on Saturday, against what it calls “Art Basel, the fair of plunder,” reports Le Monde . The French media described the social media post as “riddled with approximations and falsehoods” about how wealthy individuals are allegedly enriching themselves by buying art for supposed investment and tax-reduction purposes. article_text:
To receive Morning Links in your inbox every weekday, sign up for our Breakfast with ARTnews newsletter.

Good morning!

Ahead of planned protests in Paris and calls to demonstrate at the Grand Palais, where Art Basel is held, the fair would not confirm at this stage whether it will have to shutter Saturday, even as other art spaces, such as the Fondation Louis Vuitton, announce closures.

An early Roman-era marble torso just broke an auction record for classical sculpture, selling for $34.3 million at Sotheby’s.

The New York Public Library was gifted some 250 prints by Kiki Smith from her sister, the artist Seton Smith.

The Headlines

ART BASEL PARIS PACKING UP EARLY? Ahead of planned protests Saturday, the Fondation Louis Vuitton plans to close its doors out of precaution, ARTnews has learned. New anti-government protests about social and economic inequalities are expected in Paris and other European cities this weekend, sparking rumors that Art Basel may also have to close early as a result. Reporter Julie Brener Davich posted on Instagram that the fair stated that “at this stage we have nothing to share. We remain in close contact with the Paris Police Prefecture and all relevant authorities and will communicate any decision as soon as practicable.” ARTnews has contacted Art Basel for comment. Meanwhile, the Instagram account Documentations Art has called on readers to “take the Grand Palais,” where Art Basel is held, in a form of protest on Saturday, against what it calls “Art Basel, the fair of plunder,” reports Le Monde . The French media described the social media post as “riddled with approximations and falsehoods” about how wealthy individuals are allegedly enriching themselves by buying art for supposed investment and tax-reduction purposes. Many online comments criticized the logic behind the post, but rumors have spread of a potential protest at the fair on a day when the general public typically visits.

VENI, VIDI, VENDIDI . Following heated bidding, an early Roman-era marble torso just broke an auction record for classical sculpture, selling for $34.3 million at Sotheby’s Magnum Opus Evening Auction on Wednesday, reports ArtDependence . The torso, wearing an ornate tunic carved in incredible detail, is believed to represent one of the Julio-Claudian emperors, who ruled Rome from 27 BC to AD 68, and it was likely made in two parts to stand, with most of its weight unevenly placed on its right leg.

The Digest

The New York Public Library was gifted some 250 prints by Kiki Smith from her sister, the artist Seton Smith . [ ARTnews ]

The convicted Miami art dealer Leslie Roberts , sentenced to prison for selling fake Andy Warhols , has been assisting federal agents with investigations into other cases of art fraud. [ The Art Newspaper ]

Florentina Holzinger ’s concluding Venice Biennale performance, CLOSING ÉTUDE , is “a final dinner” that will include a procession from the Austrian pavilion to the historic Scuola Grande della Misericordia. [ ARTnews ]

Months of delays in grant payments from the San Francisco Art Commission to artists are worrying awardees, some of whom still haven’t been paid and are struggling to make ends meet as a result. [ San Francisco Examiner ]

The Swedish “museum” network Fotografiska has opened its fifth site in China, specifically the Shenzhen Bay MIXC commercial center, adding to its global expansion. [ Le Journal des Arts ]

The Kicker

WHO WANTS THE WORLD? A 1930’s globe used by General Dwight D. Eisenhower during World War II was damaged when Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dispatched his own team to relocate the artifact from the Pentagon and put it in his own office, reports the Washington Post . “Ordinarily, moving historical items within the building is a deliberate process overseen by trained curators,” explains the Post . But for whatever reason, Hegseth’s staff wanted to bypass protocol, and the people moving the 30-inch globe dropped and broke it. The Army confirmed the damage during an “attempted move” on February 3, which left a hole in the sphere. In the end, the broken globe stayed in its original place. “Hegseth wants an Eisenhower totem to be like Ike, brilliant in war and peace,” said Ty Seidule, a retired brigadier general. “Hegseth is no Ike. The globe won’t give him Ike’s attributes of humility, intellect, and judgment.”

article_text:
T his documentary is a collaboration between Justin Hardy and Dominic Hardy, two of film director Robin Hardy’s children (he had seven in all, and was married five times), and it delves into the legacy of both their father and his most enduring work, 1973 folk-horror classic The Wicker Man . The latter still stands today, for all its imperfections and peculiarities, as one of the most unsettling and paradoxically influential British films of all time, despite being a box-office flop on its initial release. This latest work is partly an account of The Wicker Man’s troubled production – a story that’s been told in books and journalism a fair few times already – and its strange reemergence as a cult movie-cum-fetish object, and partly a therapeutic exercise for the brothers themselves, full of raw feeling that’s sometimes painful to watch.

However, while the brothers’ willingness to share their pain remains admirable, their film feels hampered by omissions and silences. On some level it is haunted by the ghosts of significant players in the story who have passed away, including Hardy himself and screenwriter Anthony Shaffer, as well as other key figures who are alive but aren’t interviewed here. Where, for example, are the brothers’ other siblings? Allan Brown, author of Inside The Wicker Man: How Not to Make a Cult Classic, is mentioned in several juicy anecdotes but is also absent, while somewhat bafflingly there’s a fair amount of an interview with Scottish actor Bill Paterson, who was almost cast in the original film but wasn’t.

Of the two brothers, Justin’s is the more prominent voice; he died in August just before the festival premiere of Wrath of the Gods, a long-nurtured semi-sequel to The Wicker Man he made with Dominic. Justin comes across as a choleric, clenched figure, understandably simmering with rage at a father who walked out of his life when he was still a child, leaving him and his sister in the care of their alcoholic mother, who was effectively bankrupted by the financial failure of The Wicker Man. Dominic, born to a different mother and raised in Canada, comes across as more tender-hearted, more forgiving of his father, thanks perhaps to both physical distance and the detachment of his training as an art historian.

There’s a little, possibly unintentional, comedy to be had at one point when Dominic goes missing during filming and we see Justin raging over it to the film’s producers. The vignette stands as a salutary reminder that film-making is bloody hard work and it’s almost a miracle anything ever gets made, let alone an accidental masterpiece like The Wicker Man.

editorial_title_zh: 我们被欠下的时间：荣誉女性集体与等待政治
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在《全国等待登记册》（Registro Nacional de Espera）中，荣誉女性集体（Las Honorarias）将加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊（Galería Gabriela Mistral）变成了一个虚构但仍在运作的公共机构。其宗旨是通过一个数字平台，汇编智利各界人士在办理各种手续时的等待时间……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "在《全国等待登记册》中，荣誉女性集体将加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊变成了一个虚构但仍在运作的公共机构。其宗旨是通过一个开放的数字平台，汇编智利各界人士在办理各种手续时的等待时间。对于这个智利艺术集体而言，“等待就像是一种无声的阶级机制：它规训着谁能自由支配时间，而谁不能”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有些时间并未被官方统计数据所记录：我们在急诊室里度过的时间、在公交车站等待的时间、为了上班从城市一端奔波到另一端的时间，或者是在窗口前等待尚未办结的手续的时间。即便我们生活在一个以生产力为核心组织起来的社会里，这些小时也在没有任何补偿的情况下从我们的生活中消失了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《全国等待登记册》中，智利艺术集体“荣誉女性”（由罗埃里·埃雷拉［Roery Herrera］和洛雷托·穆尼奥斯［Loreto Muñoz］组成）将时间视为一种分配不均的特权。金钱可以让人花钱买时间，从而减少等待、缩短通勤，而那些缺乏资源的人则必须毫无报酬地承担这些时间，甚至可能因为放弃从事有报酬的活动而遭受收入损失。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该项目将加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊的空间改造成了一个虚构的公共机构，然而它却在实际运作。其宗旨是通过一个向公众开放参与的数字平台，汇编智利各地人们的等待时间。网站首页上写着：你的人生有多少时间曾被某个机构扣留？这份集体档案将等待记录为一种政治与日常生活体验。", "links": [{"text": "plataforma digital", "url": "https://registronacionaldeespera.cl/?utm_source=ig&utm_medium=social&utm_content=link_in_bio&fbclid=PAZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAcGRvZgJzcnRjBmFwcF9pZA85MzY2MTk3NDMzOTI0NTkAAaevcROB2HwX7SBKi30dvhNa4uSFTQJfSD25HUm7FoUynGfQOkfYXEByLw6Qqw_aem_nMegmsV_XQTD0k4Ynji8HA"}], "画廊橱窗里安装的一块LED屏幕上滚动显示着各项数据、它们的地域分布，以及组织该登记册的各个类别——健康、交通、住房和教育。在展厅内部，一台连续纸打印机复印着参与者发来的证词，这些证词堆积在地面上。这些零散片段的汇集，构成了一种特殊的物质档案，记录着那些通常在孤独中经历、且被所有文集排除在外的遭遇。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "该装置具有刻意营造的简陋外观。由回收纸板覆盖的木质结构、重复利用的电脑、临时凑合的家具，以及经过改造的电子设备，共同构成了一个看似临时、却渴望履行公共职能的办公室。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "官僚程序的庄严感与通常与短暂性联系在一起的一次性材料形成了鲜明对比，这是一种有效且切实的物质与概念冲突。对荣誉女性集体而言，其目标是借用国家机构的密码，去构想另一种管理方式，以此对抗官僚作风倾向于将之转化为个人问题的趋势。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "“全国等待登记册”展览现场，荣誉女性集体，加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，智利圣地亚哥，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这项作品延续了荣誉女性集体围绕劳工及其物质条件持续展开的调查。在先前的展览中，如《额头上的汗水》（2023）和《荣誉女性项目》（2024），该集体从艺术领域自身出发探讨了劳动的不稳定性，质疑了作品构思与生产作品所需劳动之间的分离。最近，在《占领》（2025）中，这种关切延伸到了劳动、空间与休息之间的关系。", "links": [{"text": "El Sudor de la Frente", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/2023/10/07/las-honorarias-con-el-sudor-de-plaza-de-armas/"}, {"text": "Proyecto Honorarias", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/2024/04/22/proyecto-honorarias-quien-trabaja-para-quien/"}, {"text": "Ocupación", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/2025/08/28/las-honorarias-el-trabajo-el-extravio-el-descanso/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《全国等待登记册》扩大了关注焦点。问题不再仅仅是谁在工作、在什么条件下工作以及为谁工作，还有谁在不工作时能够支配自己的时间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从这个意义上说，等待是劳资关系中被隐形的一个因素。在看病问诊、搭乘公共交通或寻找住房过程中浪费的时间，不一定是工作时间，但也不能被视为自由时间。它受到时间表、距离、服务可用性以及寻找替代方案的经济能力的制约。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那些能够负担私立就诊、搭乘出租车或雇人加速办手续的人，更有可能缩短等待时间。而完全依赖公共服务的人则必须让自己的生活适应系统的节奏。因此，不平等不仅表现在对资源的获取上，还表现在决定如何处理每天每小时的权力上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-031.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“全国等待登记册”展览现场，荣誉女性集体，加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，智利圣地亚哥，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-028.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“全国等待登记册”展览现场，荣誉女性集体，加布里埃拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，智利圣地亚哥，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "时间分配上的不平等也影响到了休息与闲暇。正如韩炳哲在其对功绩社会的批判中所警告的那样，自由时间同样未能逃脱生产力的要求。休息变成了为了恢复体力以重新投入工作的一个间歇，而闲暇则失去了其作为免除义务之自由时间的属性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但女性主义思想几十年来一直在指出另一种现实：对许多人而言，这种自由时间根本不曾存在。很大一部分家务和照料劳动——抚养、做饭、打扫、陪伴老人或照顾受抚养者——都是在没有报酬和没有社会认可的情况下进行的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "西尔维娅·费代里奇（Silvia Federici）等思想家曾表明，资本主义经济如何依赖于这种再生产劳动，同时又将其贬抑至一个表面上与生产无关的领域。从这一视角来看，等待呈现出另一种复杂性，因为它不仅剥夺了可用的小时数，还加剧了支撑他人生活的任务分配不公。对于陪伴孩子就诊的母亲，或是照顾老人的照料者而言，拖延打断或延长了一个在义务与休息之间可能已无清晰界限的工作日。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉斯·奥诺里亚斯的这个项目也可以结合马克·费舍尔（Mark Fisher）的《资本主义现实主义》（Realismo capitalista）来解读，他关于政治想象力局限性的反思将等待置于日常挫折之外。如果现行的经济秩序呈现为一种难以变革的现实，我们也往往将其延误、无休止的官僚程序以及一再推迟的承诺视为不可避免。等待被自然化了。人们学会了与它共存，它迫使我们重新安排日常生活、取消其他活动，并在等待一个可能需要数月或数年才能轮到的号子时推迟各种需求。未来解决方案的承诺与不知何时到来的无力感并存。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "面对这种常态化，拉斯·奥诺里亚斯提出了一种虚构的制度，它并不旨在从行政层面解决问题，而是通过艺术将问题暴露出来，并试图改变我们的感知方式。反等待委员会（CAE）由艺术二人组于2025年发起，源自他们在等待成为常态的地方——诊所、车站和公共办公室——所进行的聚会。“街头下午茶”（onces callejeras）将不同社区的人们聚集在一起，谈论他们的经历，并共同思考失去的时间如何影响他们的生活。在加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊呈现的登记正是诞生于这些对话，并力求通过一个能够汇集原本会四分五裂的经验的装置来延续它们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-065.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "智利艺术家团体拉斯·奥诺里亚斯（Las Honorarias）的展览《国家等待登记》（Registro Nacional de Espera）现场，智利圣地亚哥加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-075.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "智利艺术家团体拉斯·奥诺里亚斯（Las Honorarias）的展览《国家等待登记》（Registro Nacional de Espera）现场，智利圣地亚哥加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "公众的参与对作品的运作至关重要。输入自己数据的人不再仅仅是旁观者，而是变成了信息的生产者，并有可能成为围绕等待问题组织起来的社区成员。反等待委员会的会议室配有旗帜、破碎的沙漏、布告栏、简陋的印刷品、宣言的分发以及调解活动，具有超出单纯数据收集的集会和煽动性质。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在反等待委员会的宣言中，该团体断言“等待是一种前卡特尔化（precarización）的方式”和“无休止的排号是一种遗忘的形式”。第二句话指向了一个超越程序中隐含的耽搁的后果，因为当一种需求无限期地悬而未决时，对其采取行动的可能性也被推迟了。我们留在了行政的灰色地带，并伴随着沮丧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因为等待的时间不仅被白白消磨，它还会消磨申诉、重组生活以及规划未来的能力。正因如此，“如果在我们的一生中权利不再需要排队，我们会做些什么”这一问题不仅关乎公共服务的效率：它质问的是时间的根本分配方式，以及让某些人能够支配时间而另一些人必须将时间交由等待的种种条件。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉斯·奥诺里亚斯的项目汇聚了通常以个人方式经历的种种体验，并使未被计算的巨量流失时间清晰可见。然而，这种可见性本身并不能保证产生等待的条件发生改变，也无法保证针对这些等待形成集体回应。要求《国家等待登记》在政治上产生其创作者未必赋予它的实际影响，将是不切实际的。它既不呼吁人们逆来顺受地接受被剥夺的时间，其发明的机构也无法将这些时间还给我们。相反，它能帮助我们去质问：我们究竟学会了无条件地交出多少生命中的存在，甚至连原因都不曾过问。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-068.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "智利艺术家团体拉斯·奥诺里亚斯（Las Honorarias）的展览《国家等待登记》（Registro Nacional de Espera）现场，智利圣地亚哥加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-070.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "智利艺术家团体拉斯·奥诺里亚斯（Las Honorarias）的展览《国家等待登记》（Registro Nacional de Espera）现场，智利圣地亚哥加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊，2026年。摄影：马蒂亚斯·波夫莱特·阿拉维纳（Matías Poblete Aravena）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家团体拉斯·奥诺里亚斯的《国家等待登记》将在智利圣地亚哥阿拉米达1381号的加夫列拉·米斯特拉尔画廊展出至2026年11月7日。", "links": [{"text": "Galería Gabriela Mistral", "url": "https://galeriagm.cultura.gob.cl/"}], "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "En Registro Nacional de Espera , Las Honorarias transforman la Galería Gabriela Mistral en una institución pública ficticia pero operativa. Su propósito es compilar los tiempos de espera de personas que realizan diversos trámites en Chile mediante una plataforma digital abierta. Para el colectivo chileno, “la espera funciona como un mecanismo silencioso de clase: organiza quién puede disponer libremente de su tiempo y quién no”."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Hay un tiempo que no registran las estadísticas oficiales: el que pasamos en una sala de urgencias, en un paradero, trasladándonos de un extremo a otro de la ciudad para llegar al trabajo, o frente a una ventanilla en un trámite que no termina de resolverse. Son horas que desaparecen de nuestras vidas sin compensación alguna, aun cuando vivimos en una sociedad organizada en torno a la productividad."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "En Registro Nacional de Espera , el colectivo chileno Las Honorarias —integrado por Roery Herrera y Loreto Muñoz — aborda el tiempo como un privilegio distribuido de manera desigual. El dinero permite pagar para reducir las esperas y acortar los traslados, mientras que quienes no cuentan con recursos deben asumir esas horas sin retribución alguna, e incluso pueden perder ingresos al dejar de realizar una actividad remunerada."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "El proyecto convierte el espacio de la Galería Gabriela Mistral en una institución pública ficticia que, sin embargo, está operativa. Su propósito es compilar los tiempos de espera de personas de distintos lugares de Chile mediante una plataforma digital abierta a la participación. En la portada del sitio web, se lee: ¿Cuánto tiempo de su vida ha sido retenido por una institución? Este archivo colectivo registra la espera como experiencia política y cotidiana.", "links": [{"text": "plataforma digital", "url": "https://registronacionaldeespera.cl/?utm_source=ig&utm_medium=social&utm_content=link_in_bio&fbclid=PAZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAcGRvZgJzcnRjBmFwcF9pZA85MzY2MTk3NDMzOTI0NTkAAaevcROB2HwX7SBKi30dvhNa4uSFTQJfSD25HUm7FoUynGfQOkfYXEByLw6Qqw_aem_nMegmsV_XQTD0k4Ynji8HA"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "En una pantalla LED instalada en la vitrina de la galería, y visible desde la calle, se despliegan las cifras, su distribución territorial y las categorías -salud, transporte, vivienda y educación- que organizan el registro. En el interior, una impresora de papel continuo reproduce los testimonios enviados por los participantes, que se amontonan en el suelo. La suma de estos fragmentos compone una suerte de archivo material de aquello que, por lo general, se vive en soledad y queda fuera de todo compendio."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-020.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Vista de la exposición Registro Nacional de Espera , del colectivo Las Honorarias, en la Galería Gabriela Mistral, Santiago de Chile, 2026. Foto:  Matías Poblete Aravena", "credit": "Artishock"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Las-Honorarias_Registro-Nacional-de-Espera-024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Vista de la exposición Registro Nacional de Espera , del colectivo Las Honorarias, en la Galería Gabriela Mistral, Santiago de Chile, 2026. article_text:
En Registro Nacional de Espera , Las Honorarias transforman la Galería Gabriela Mistral en una institución pública ficticia pero operativa. Su propósito es compilar los tiempos de espera de personas que realizan diversos trámites en Chile mediante una plataforma digital abierta. Para el colectivo chileno, “la espera funciona como un mecanismo silencioso de clase: organiza quién puede disponer libremente de su tiempo y quién no”.

Hay un tiempo que no registran las estadísticas oficiales: el que pasamos en una sala de urgencias, en un paradero, trasladándonos de un extremo a otro de la ciudad para llegar al trabajo, o frente a una ventanilla en un trámite que no termina de resolverse. Son horas que desaparecen de nuestras vidas sin compensación alguna, aun cuando vivimos en una sociedad organizada en torno a la productividad.

En Registro Nacional de Espera , el colectivo chileno Las Honorarias —integrado por Roery Herrera y Loreto Muñoz — aborda el tiempo como un privilegio distribuido de manera desigual. El dinero permite pagar para reducir las esperas y acortar los traslados, mientras que quienes no cuentan con recursos deben asumir esas horas sin retribución alguna, e incluso pueden perder ingresos al dejar de realizar una actividad remunerada.

El proyecto convierte el espacio de la Galería Gabriela Mistral en una institución pública ficticia que, sin embargo, está operativa. Su propósito es compilar los tiempos de espera de personas de distintos lugares de Chile mediante una plataforma digital abierta a la participación. En la portada del sitio web, se lee: ¿Cuánto tiempo de su vida ha sido retenido por una institución? Este archivo colectivo registra la espera como experiencia política y cotidiana.

En una pantalla LED instalada en la vitrina de la galería, y visible desde la calle, se despliegan las cifras, su distribución territorial y las categorías -salud, transporte, vivienda y educación- que organizan el registro. En el interior, una impresora de papel continuo reproduce los testimonios enviados por los participantes, que se amontonan en el suelo. La suma de estos fragmentos compone una suerte de archivo material de aquello que, por lo general, se vive en soledad y queda fuera de todo compendio.

La instalación tiene una apariencia deliberadamente precaria. Estructuras de madera recubiertas de cartón reciclado, computadores reutilizados, mobiliario improvisado y dispositivos electrónicos alterados configuran una oficina que parece provisional, aunque aspira a desempeñar una función pública.

La solemnidad de los procedimientos burocráticos contrasta con materiales desechables que suelen asociarse a lo transitorio, una contradicción material y conceptual efectiva. Para Las Honorarias, el objetivo es apropiarse de los códigos de una institución estatal para imaginar otra forma de administrar lo que la tramitología tiende a convertir en un problema individual.

La obra continúa una investigación que el colectivo Las Honorarias viene desarrollando en torno al trabajo y sus condiciones materiales. En exposiciones anteriores, como El Sudor de la Frente (2023) y Proyecto Honorarias (2024), el colectivo abordó la precariedad laboral desde el propio campo artístico, cuestionando la separación entre la concepción de una obra y el trabajo necesario para producirla. Más recientemente, en Ocupación (2025), esa preocupación se extendió a la relación entre trabajo, espacio y descanso.

Registro Nacional de Espera amplía el foco. El problema ya no es únicamente quién trabaja, en qué condiciones y para quién, sino también quién puede disponer de su tiempo cuando no está trabajando.

La espera es, en este sentido, un factor invisibilizado de las relaciones laborales. El tiempo que se pierde en una consulta médica, en el transporte público o en la búsqueda de una vivienda no es necesariamente tiempo de trabajo, pero tampoco puede considerarse tiempo libre. Está condicionado por los horarios, las distancias, la disponibilidad de servicios y la capacidad económica para encontrar alternativas.

Quien puede pagar una consulta privada, tomar un taxi o contratar a alguien que agilice un trámite tiene mayores posibilidades de acortar la espera. Quien depende exclusivamente de los servicios públicos debe acomodar su vida a los tiempos del sistema. La desigualdad se expresa así no solo en el acceso a los recursos, sino también en la posibilidad de decidir qué hacer con las horas de cada día.

La desigualdad en la distribución del tiempo también afecta al descanso y al ocio. Como advierte Byung-Chul Han en su crítica a la sociedad del rendimiento, el tiempo libre tampoco queda fuera de las exigencias de productividad. El descanso se convierte en una pausa para recuperar fuerzas y volver a trabajar, mientras el ocio pierde su condición de tiempo libre de obligaciones.

Pero hay otra realidad que el pensamiento feminista viene señalando desde hace décadas: para muchas personas, ese tiempo libre nunca llega a existir. Buena parte del trabajo doméstico y de cuidados —criar, cocinar, limpiar, acompañar a una persona mayor o atender a alguien dependiente— se realiza sin remuneración ni reconocimiento social.

Silvia Federici , entre otras pensadoras, ha mostrado cómo la economía capitalista depende de ese trabajo reproductivo, al tiempo que lo relega a una esfera aparentemente ajena a la producción. Desde esta perspectiva, la espera adquiere otra complejidad, pues no solo resta horas disponibles, sino que se suma a una distribución desigual de las tareas que sostienen la vida de otros. Para una madre que acompaña a su hijo a una consulta o para quien cuida a una persona mayor, la demora interrumpe o prolonga una jornada de trabajo que probablemente ya no tiene límites claros entre la obligación y el descanso.

El proyecto de Las Honorarias también puede leerse a la luz de Realismo capitalista , de Mark Fisher , cuya reflexión sobre los límites de la imaginación política sitúa a la espera más allá de la frustración cotidiana. Si el orden económico vigente se presenta como una realidad difícil de transformar, también tendemos a aceptar como inevitables sus demoras, sus trámites interminables y sus promesas postergadas. La espera se naturaliza. Se aprende a convivir con ella, nos fuerza a reorganizar la jornada o a cancelar otras actividades y a posponer necesidades mientras llega un turno que puede tardar meses o años. La promesa de una solución futura convive con la imposibilidad de saber cuándo llegará.

Frente a esa normalización, Las Honorarias proponen una ficción institucional que no pretende resolver administrativamente el problema, sino exponerlo a través del arte y buscar modificar cómo lo percibimos. El Comité Anti Espera (CAE) , impulsado por el dúo de artistas en 2025, surgió de encuentros realizados en lugares donde la espera forma parte de la rutina, en consultorios, paraderos y oficinas públicas. Las llamadas «onces callejeras» reunieron a personas de distintas comunidades para conversar sobre sus experiencias y pensar colectivamente cómo el tiempo perdido afecta sus vidas. El registro presentado en la Galería Gabriela Mistral nace de esas conversaciones y busca darles continuidad mediante un dispositivo capaz de reunir experiencias que, de otro modo, permanecerían dispersas.

La participación del público es fundamental para el funcionamiento de la obra. Quien ingresa sus datos deja de ser únicamente espectador para volverse productor de información y, potencialmente, integrante de una comunidad organizada en torno al problema de la espera. La sala de reuniones del Comité Anti Espera, con sus banderas, su reloj de arena roto, una cartelera, una prensa precaria, la distribución del manifiesto y las actividades de mediación, tiene un carácter asambleario y agitador que va más allá de la mera recopilación de datos.

En el manifiesto del Comité Anti Espera, el colectivo afirma que «las esperas son un modo de precarización» y que «el turno eterno es una forma de olvido». La segunda frase apunta a una consecuencia que supera la demora implícita en el trámite, ya que cuando una necesidad permanece indefinidamente pendiente, también se posterga la posibilidad de actuar sobre ella. Nos quedamos en el limbo administrativo, y con frustración.

Y es que el tiempo de espera no solo se pierde; puede desgastar la capacidad de reclamar, reorganizar la vida y proyectar un futuro. Por eso, la pregunta de qué haríamos con una vida donde los derechos no tuvieran fila de espera no remite únicamente a la eficiencia de los servicios públicos: interroga la distribución misma del tiempo y las condiciones que permiten a unas personas disponer de él mientras otras deben entregarlo a la espera.

El proyecto de Las Honorarias congrega experiencias que suelen vivirse de manera individual y hace visible la magnitud de un tiempo perdido que no se contabiliza. Esa visibilidad, sin embargo, no garantiza por sí sola cambios en las condiciones que producen las esperas ni una respuesta colectiva frente a ellas. Sería desproporcionado exigirle a Registro Nacional de Espera una indicencia real en la política que sus creadoras no necesariamente le atribuyen. Ni clama por la resignación a las horas robadas, ni la institución que se inventa puede devolvernos ese tiempo. Puede, en cambio, ayudarnos a cuestionar cuánto de nuestra existencia hemos aprendido a ceder sin siquiera preguntarnos por qué.

Registro Nacional de Espera , del colectivo Las Honorarias, estará abierta hasta el 7 de noviembre de 2026 en la Galería Gabriela Mistral , Alameda 1381, Santiago de Chile.

article_text:
T hink back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up , Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI . And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

In Musk’s version, as the tale begins Odysseus is – off screen – pretending to be mad to avoid fighting in the Trojan war. Grim-faced Palamedes and Agamemnon are shown testing this ruse by taking his baby boy Telemachus and placing him in the harm’s way of a plough in a field; Odysseus instantly rushes to save his child, showing that he isn’t mad, and agrees to fight. We see him join the armada, with Penelope and Telemachus (soon to grow to a little boy) left behind. This, effectively, is a prologue sequence that is not in Nolan. The expeditionary force arrives at Troy, and an intertitle tells us we have cut to a 10-years-later flashforward; the siege is about to escalate into the fake-horse attack.

As ever, the AI footage is ponderous and inert, demonstrating its familiar uncanny-valley stock-footage quality with classical-age Call of Duty graphics. Every single dramatic moment – Odysseus’s cod-insanity and his agreeing to fight, taking leave of his family, the hardship and adventure of the sea journey and the climactic decision – is all as motiveless and meaningless as the movement of shapes on a laptop screensaver. The ships are lined up on the sea like a row of high-def space invaders. Perhaps the worst thing about it is the deadly audio and digital-robot voice work. Every character speaks with that even, over-emphatic, declamatory tone.

Who cares? Certainly not Musk. He has no passion to tell us this story, only to win an argument that he long since lost. Perhaps he will now do his Grok AI version of Digger, in which Tom Cruise’s oil baron in fact saves the universe by drilling for more and yet more oil. Or maybe he will release his own Grok AI version of You Can See Everything in which glassy-eyed Elizabeth Holmes will prove her little blood-diagnosis box actually does work before she zooms off with Elon in his flying car.

Of course, as we are always being told, AI is continuously improving. With succeeding episodes, this boring and pointless series may look better. But if Elon’s AI-Odyssey is of any value at all, it is to underscore the basic truth: nobody believes AI has any artistic merit, only financial merit. In terms of quality, it is a pitiful fraction of the real thing, but a zillionth of a zillionth of a zillionth of the cost. It is time for Elon to make his own inglorious retreat from this phoney AI Dull-yssey.

岡田 敦｜幻の馬 Yururi Island 1950-2026

2026.12.1 （火） — 2027.1.17 （日）

開催期間：2026年12月1日（火） ～ 2027年1月17日（日）

休館日：毎週月曜日（月曜日が祝休日の場合は開館し、翌平日休館）

料金：一般1,200円(960円)、学生・65歳以上950円(760円)、小中高生400円(320円) ※( )は有料入場者20名以上の団体料金 ※未就学児、障害者手帳をお持ちの方とその介護者(２名まで)は無料 ※第３水曜日は65歳以上無料 ※各種割引の併用はできません

ユルリ島は現代の“ロスト・ワールド”である。この言葉はコナン・ドイルが著した、断崖に囲まれた人跡未踏の台地に絶滅したはずの動物たちの王国があったという空想小説のタイトルだが、ユルリ島という無人島もまた、立ち入りが制限されて人は近づけない。そしてここには人知れず馬たちが、それも雌馬だけが暮らしているのだ。岡田敦はそんなロスト・ワールドの目撃者である。雌馬だけとなった群れは誕生の可能性を持たず、1950年に島に移入された馬の子孫は岡田が撮影を始めた2011年には10数頭、そして今は２頭にまで減った。この展覧会で見られる写真に刻印されているのは、いわば蝋燭の炎が消えんとする瞬間の揺めきだ。その儚くも美しい命の証の光が人々の記憶に残ることを願う。 Yururi Island ラムダプリント ユルリ島 根室半島・昆布盛漁港の南東2.6㎞の沖合にあり、周囲（海岸線長）7.8㎞、面積1.98㎢。1950年、北方領土を追われた人々が馬を連れて島に移住。漁撈環境の整備とともに島民が去ると島には馬だけが残された。現在は国指定鳥獣保護区（特別保護地区）、北海道指定天然記念物、北海道自然環境保全地域などに登録され、立ち入りは制限されている。 Yururi Island, July 2018 ラムダプリント

見どころ

その１ 15年間のまなざしの集大成

2011 年からユルリ島の馬を撮り続けた岡田敦の静かなる情熱の軌跡―。その 集大成となる本展は、東京の美術館で開催する初の大規模展です。

写真作品約80点、映像作品２点、関連資料を展示します。

その２ 消えゆく命の記録に立ち会う

上陸を許された岡田が撮影した厳しくも美しいユルリ島の自然と、馬と共に暮らした時代の薄れゆく記憶。いま留めておくべき光景に出会う展示です。

その３ 新作を初公開

本展では最後の2頭となったユルリ島の馬の姿を新たに捉えた未発表作品のほか、島の対岸にあたる根室半島で撮影された新作を初公開します。

岡田 敦

写真家、芸術学博士。1979年生まれ、北海道出身。大阪芸術大学芸術学部写真学科卒、東京工芸大学大学院芸術学研究科博士後期課程修了。富士フォトサロン新人賞、木村伊兵衛写真賞、北海道文化奨励賞、東川賞特別作家賞、JRA賞馬事文化賞を受賞。主な写真集に『I am』(赤々舎)、『ataraxia』(青幻舎)、『世界』(赤々舎)、『MOTHER』(柏艪舎)、『エピタフ 幻の島、ユルリの光跡』(インプレス)、『The Horses of Yururi Island ユルリ島の馬』(青幻舎)がある。作品は北海道立近代美術館、神田日勝記念美術館、東川町文化ギャラリー、東京工芸大学写大ギャラリーにパブリックコレクションされている。

article_text:
The first look at Greta Gerwig ’s vision for Narnia has been revealed.

Today, Netflix is giving a first look at her vision for CS Lewis ’s magical world in the trailer for The Magician’s Nephew, the first chronological book in the beloved series.

With the soundtrack of Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven, the trailer opens with magician Andrew Ketterley ( Daniel Craig ) intoning that “sometimes one story is the beginning to all the others”, as he gives a group of kids a magic ring that will transport them to strange and wonderful lands.

Elsewhere, the trailer gives a first look at many locations and characters familiar to fans, including Jadis (Emma Mackey, the future White Witch) and Aslan, the mythical lion voiced by Meryl Streep .

The Magician’s Nephew tells the story of two children in Edwardian England named Digory and Polly (newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell) who chance upon the Wood Between Worlds, a realm with many portals to different dimensions. There, they witness the birth of Narnia.

In a trailer premiere event in New York this morning, Gerwig spoke of her longtime passion for CS Lewis’s series. “I don’t remember a time I didn’t know the books,” she said, per Variety . “I wouldn’t be who I am without these books.”

The film, which is Gerwig’s first since her $1bn-grossing megahit Barbie , will open for an eight-week theatrical window on 12 February before it streams on Netflix starting 2 April, in the studio’s first global theatrical release.

“I told Ted [Sarandos, CEO of Netflix] I only know how to make movies for the big screen,” Gerwig said. “He said: ‘Make the movie for the biggest screen and trust the process.’”

The director added that she petitioned Led Zeppelin’s Robert Plant and Jimmy Page for permission to use Stairway to Heaven in the trailer.

“I talked to them about a lot of the themes of the film,” Gerwig said, as reported by Rolling Stone . “They saw the heart and the story and the drama in it.”

“It’s an epic song,” she added. “It’s about the two paths of good and evil … It is a spiritual quest and a spiritual journey. So to me, this was a song that made sense to introduce the film to the world.”

"那些“不知情”者的数量远远超过了少数“知情”者（其中包括以三种不同造型出场的拜伦·科恩本人）。有些人或许确实会觉得这一切令人作呕，但我认为它有其必要性；尽管并非每个包袱都响了，但其中足够多的高能场面依然让人惊掉下巴，甚至让人纳闷他到底是怎么在没有中途被人谋杀的情况下完成这一切的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在时隔24年后，Ali G 回归了。他是一个文化挪用成性的伦敦白人，坚信自己是带有牙买加血统的黑人，并且总是穿着成那样四处招摇以证明这一点。这个角色最初为1998年的《11点档秀》（11 O’Clock Show）而创，后来登陆 HBO 的《Da Ali G Show》，甚至在2002年推出了电影《Ali G进豪宅》（Ali G Indahouse）。在如今这个黑暗时期，拜伦·科恩显然认为时机已到，以精湛的讽刺形式将他重新带回大众视野，因为自从他上次露面以来，世界已经进一步陷入了深渊。在此期间虽然曾有波罗（Bruno），尤其是波拉特（Borat），但 Ali G（即阿利斯泰尔·莱斯利·格雷厄姆，Alistair Leslie Graham）才是笑点界的元祖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影开场时银幕上出现了一句话：“能让你相信荒谬事物的人，就能让你制造暴行。”这正是拜伦·科恩与其5人编剧团队构思出的“剧本”中所发生的事情。在片中，Ali G 正为 HBO 打算邀请他录制该节目第三季的前景而飘飘然，完全没意识到这个“邀约”早在22年前就已经过期了。没错，他是个白痴。但这并不妨碍他组建一个团队（“不知情”），招募经纪人加尔·莱斯特（Gar Lester，“不知情”），并大办了一场价值12,000美元的晚宴来庆祝。他还和自己大腹便便的女友朱莉（由摩根·罗宾逊饰演，表现惊艳且放得开）一起庆祝。朱莉幻想着即将到来的大笔资金注入，便请了一位状况外的豪华比弗利山庄房地产经纪人（“不知情”）带他们去看一套价值3000万美元、面积19,000平方英尺的待售豪宅。这是片中最精彩的片段之一，你不得不佩服这位经纪人，他当时一定非常渴望成交这笔买卖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，没有钱，也没有节目。Ali G 打给 HBO 的卡西·布洛伊斯（Casey Bloys）办公室的电话全无回音。但该怎么办呢？孩子就要出生了。他尝试去干一些底层杂货，比如在农场干活，却十分搞笑地一无所获。不过希望总是常存，当 Ali G 误读了一位名叫罗基（Rocky，由克莱夫·拉塞尔饰）的猫王模仿者发来的急电时，他误以为这条信息证实了自己实际上是说唱巨星 A$AP Rocky 的儿子（A$AP Rocky本人并未参演该片，但出现在片尾字幕中，且与蕾哈娜一同属于“知情”人员）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片的前半部分包含了一系列与“不知情”者的遭遇，其中包括一名多元、平等与包容（DEI）教练、一位顺势疗法医生、一名试图警告他不要服用过多类似伟哥药物的酒类商店员工（我们当场就能看到明显的效果），诸如此类。拜伦·科恩还化身成了一个名叫尼拉·凯恩·恩德杰奥切洛（Nira Cain N’Degeocello）的极左进步派人士，他穿着比尔·科斯比（Cosby）风格的毛衣，在奥克兰一个社区中心的满屋黑人维权人士面前发表长篇大论，警告他们文化挪用者阿里·G正在逍遥法外，必须予以制止。他成了旨在阻止阿里·G的主要死敌。他向这群（全都是“不知情”的）人讲述了自己写的书《我有一个更好的梦想》（I Have A Better Dream），并称RAP实际上代表“激进非洲诗歌”（Radical African Poetry），随后除了一个人之外，几乎所有人都成群结队地退场了。另一个精选场景是恩德杰奥切洛向聚集在一个小学开放日的家长们（全都是“不知情”的）发表讲话，向他们通报学校旨在为所有孩子设立“强制性别逆转年试验”的项目。“你是说我得看着我儿子像个女孩一样穿一年衣服？”一个愤怒的父亲尖叫道。恩德杰奥切洛更进一步称，如果这“行得通”，他们可以将其变成永久性的：小蒂米可以拥有金·卡戴珊（Kim Kardashian）的臀部，而小夏洛特可以拥有奥兰多·布鲁姆（Orlando Bloom）的生殖器。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片由一个又一个段子组成，有些略显刻意搞笑，但其中足够多的笑料发挥了作用，让人感觉这是一部典型的拜伦·科恩式冒险喜剧，专门拿那些毫无所知的人开涮。不过，真正的重头戏在后半部分，拜伦·科恩又推出了另一个角色——前摩萨德反恐专家埃兰·莫拉德（Erran Morrad）。他召集了一群热爱特朗普的“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）拥趸执行终极任务：他们必须阻止这个名叫亚历杭德罗·冈萨雷斯（Alejandro Gonzales，实际上是阿里·G）的墨西哥罪犯，此人已孕育了140,000个孩子，以此确保他们出生在美国本土，从而用移民淹没这个国家。纽特·金里奇（Newt Gingrich）以及共和党国会议员安迪·哈里斯（Andy Harris）和拉尔夫·诺曼（Ralph Norman）（都是“不知情”的）竟然深信不疑，并录制了公益广告（PSA）来警告他的存在和计划。莫拉德为这群人（全都是“不知情”的）每人配备了一个假臀部，可以通过假阴茎触发发射子弹，随后准备好让他们去抓捕朱莉即将出生的孩子，将其送到直升机垂下的绳索座椅上，并立即将其运送到边境对面。整个这一段必须亲眼目睹才能相信，但它证明了拜伦·科恩试图表达的终极观点。警惕极端主义——来自双方（左翼也未能幸免）。这是一个危险的时代，外面有很多疯子，他们大多在看福克斯新闻（Fox News）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个涉及身败名裂的国会议员乔治·桑托斯（George Santos）（“不知情”）积极参与的桥段是如此毫无品味、如此卑劣，以至于我不想在这里描述它。但令人不寒而栗的是，整个电视制作团队（同样是“不知情”）以及包括桑托斯在内的其他人，竟然会在极度低俗的《言论自由秀》（The Free Speech Show，这是阿里·G获得的一个主持工作）的一个大屠杀主题小品中实际参与这种事情。这简直让人头晕目眩，拜伦·科恩将其推到了边缘——甚至超越了边缘——然后才让阿里·G惊恐地走开。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《阿里·G：我是谁？》（Ali G: Who Iz I?）实际上，通过其主演的所有滑稽动作、所有夸张的笑料和精心策划的恶作剧，以及所有让人大跌眼镜的奇妙事实——即大多数“不知情”的人居然生活在同一个星球上，并且签署了豁免书让我们观看他们的愚蠢行为——好吧，这让我不禁思考我们究竟是谁，以及在特朗普时代的今天，我们要花多长时间才能爬出我们发现自己身处其中的这个可怕兔子洞。这些人竟然是真实的，这着实有些令人沮丧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哦，是的，我确实笑了很多。拜伦·科恩在完成了自己的导演处女作后表示，这是他绝对最后一次做这种事。结束了。这很难完成而且太危险了。我不确定我是不是相信他。他会不会又在对我们所有人搞恶作剧？这种喜剧实际上是一项公共服务，所以我希望他不要在这个世界变得如此疯狂疯狂疯狂疯狂之际，正当人们最需要它来无情地展示这一现实的时候放弃它。", "translated": true}, {"type": article_text:
After I saw Sacha Baron Cohen ‘s latest mind-bending comedy Ali G: Who Iz I? , I immediately thought that this movie is proof there should be a brand new Oscar category created, for Best Clearances. The fact that there is someone out there who could actually get all the real unsuspecting morons who participated in this movie to sign off on it afterwards is simply astonishing considering what they are asked to do in it. So before going into detail on all of that, hats off to Stu Miller, Alexis Sampietro, Jordan Cohen, and Ian Phillips, and at least what I can tell by reading the end credits, Ashley Kravitz of Clearances by Ashley Inc.

And while we are on it, let’s acknowledge casting director Sarah Crowe and her team for finding these extremist idiots who make up the most incredulous parts of the movie, as well as Russell Smith Claims Counsel and the nine lawyers representing the movie. “No real person or entity depicted or appearing in the film has sponsored or otherwise endorsed its content” is the disclaimer meant to quash lawsuits.

Watch on Deadline

Sacha Baron Cohen Secret Movie Unveiled: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Hitting Theaters In October From Amazon MGM Studios

‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Writer Defends Amazon Movie Amid Outcry Over Sacha Baron Cohen’s Character Reinforcing “Harmful” Racial Stereotypes

At the end of the film there is a separation shown on screen between the characters who were “in on it” and those who were “not in on it,” meaning the real people unaware (incredibly) of who Ali G is or that they are dealing with master prankster Baron Cohen, who has won Golden Globes and Oscar nominations for pulling off the impossible, pretty much guaranteed to stir controversy, offend lots of people, but most importantly make us laugh while pointing to the truly dangerous environment of extremism, hate, misinformation, and other terrible cancers currently on our society.

The number of those “not in on it” far outweighs the handful, including Baron Cohen in three different guises, who are “in on it.” Some may indeed find this all abhorrent, but I found it necessary, and though not everything lands here, enough of it is jaw-dropping enough to make us wonder how he pulled this all off without getting murdered along the way.

After 24 years Ali G is back, a culturally appropriating white Londoner who believes he is Black with Jamaican ancestry and goes around dressed like that to prove it. Created for the 1998 11 O’Clock Show , then later for HBO’s Da Ali G Show and even a movie in 2002’s Ali G Indahouse, Baron Cohen in these dark times obviously believes the moment is right to bring him back in fine satirical form as the world has only sunk further into the abyss since his last appearance. In the meantime there has been Bruno and especially Borat, but Ali G (aka Alistair Leslie Graham) is the LOL OG.

The film begins with a phrase on screen: “Those who can make you believe absurdities can make you commit atrocities.” That is exactly what happens in the “script” dreamed up by Baron Cohen and his gaggle of five writers, in which Ali G is stoked over the prospect HBO wants to offer him a third season of his show, not realizing the “offer” expired 22 years ago. Yes, he’s an idiot. But it doesn’t stop him from putting together a crew (“not in on it”), enlisting talent agent Gar Lester (“not in on it”) and throwing a $12,000 dinner to celebrate. He also celebrates with his very pregnant girlfriend Julie (a terrific and game Morgan Robinson) who, dreaming of the new cash infusion, enlists a clueless high-end Beverly Hills realtor (“not in on it”) to show them a $30 million, 19,000-square-foot home to buy. This is one of the best bits in the movie and you have to hand it to this realtor who must have really wanted this sale.

However there is no money, and no show. Ali G’s calls to the office of HBO’s Casey Bloys go unreturned. But what to do? The baby is on the way. His attempts at menial jobs, like one on a farm, hilariously go nowhere. Hope springs eternal though when Ali G misreads a message from an Elvis impersonator named Rocky (Clive Russell) who needs to talk to him ASAP. He somehow believes this message confirms he is actually the son of rap superstar A$AP Rocky (not in the movie but in the end credits and “in on it” with Rhianna).

The first half of the film contain a series of encounters of people “not in on it” including a DEI coach, a synergistic doctor, a liquor store employee trying to warn him about taking too much of a Viagra-like substance (we get visible results right there), and on and on. Baron Cohen also appears as an extreme progressive named Nira Cain N’Degeocello, who wears Cosby-type sweaters and lectures a room full of Black activists at an Oakland Community Center, warning them that cultural appropriator Ali G is on the loose and must be stopped. He becomes the main nemesis out to stop Ali G. He tells this group (all “not in on it”) about the book he has written, “I Have A Better Dream,” and that RAP actually means “Radical African Poetry” before just about all of them, save one, walk out in droves. Another choice scene has N’Degeocello speaking to a group of parents (all of them “not in on it”) gathered for an elementary school open house and informing them of the school’s program to institute a “compulsory gender reversal year trial” for all their children. “You mean I have to watch my son dress like a girl for a year?” screams one angry father. N’Degeocello goes further, saying if it “sticks” they can make it permanent: Little Timmy can have Kim Kardashian’s buttocks, and little Charlotte can have Orlando Bloom’s genitals.

The film drifts from bit to bit, some straining for laughs but enough of it working to make this feel like vintage Baron Cohen daredevil comedy at the expense of the clueless. The real stunners though are in the second half with yet another Baron Cohen character introduced, ex-Mossad anti-terrorist expert Erran Morrad, who assembles a group of Trump-loving MAGA-ites for the ultimate mission: They must stop this Mexican criminal known as Alejandro Gonzales (actually Ali G) who has fathered 140,000 children in order to make sure they are born on American soil, thus flooding the country with immigrants. Newt Gingrich and Republican congressmen Andy Harris and Ralph Norman (“not in on it”) incredibly believe all this and tape PSAs warning of his existence and plans. Equipping each of the group (none of them “in on it”) with a prosthetic butt that fires bullets triggered by a prosthetic penis, Morrad prepares them to capture Julia’s about-to-be-born baby, deliver it to a helicopter’s dangling rope chair and transport it immediately across the border. This entire sequence simply has to be seen to be believed but it proves the ultimate point Baron Cohen is trying to make. Beware of extremism — on both sides (the left is not unskewered). These are dangerous times and there are a lot of nuts out there, mostly watching Fox News.

Another sequence involving the active participation of disgraced congressman George Santos (“not in on it”) is so tasteless, so vile, I won’t describe it here. But it is chilling to know that a whole TV production team (also “not in on it”) and others including Santos in a Holocaust-themed sketch on the ultra tacky The Free Speech Show (a hosting gig Ali G gets) would actually participate in such a thing. It is just head-spinning stuff, and Baron Cohen takes it right to the edge — and over — before having Ali G walk off in horror.

Ali G: Who Iz I? actually, through all the antics of its star, all the over-the-top gags and elaborate pranks, all the head-scratching wonderment that most of the people “not in on it” live on the same planet and signed waivers to let us watch their idiocy, well, it makes me wonder who iz we , and how long will it take to climb out of this frightening rabbit hole we find ourselves in now in the age of Trump. That these people are real is kinda depressing.

Oh, and yes I did laugh a lot. Baron Cohen, after making his own directorial debut with this one, says this is the absolute last time he is doing this kind of thing. It’s over. It’s hard to pull off and too dangerous. I am not sure I believe him. Could he be pranking all of us again? This kind of comedy is actually a public service, so I hope he doesn’t give it up just when it is needed most to savagely show how mad mad mad mad this world has become.

Ali G: Who Iz I? opens Friday for one weekend only, and beyond that will surface on Amazon’s Prime Video at a still unannounced date.

Producers are Baron Cohen and Petr Jakl. A credit at the end of the film intriguingly thanks Gar Lester “for not suing.”

article_text:
Four new members have been added to Documenta 16 ’s curatorial team headed by Naomi Beckwith , the German quinquennial has announced.

The additional members are Diné artist and composer Raven Chacon , who will join the team as its curator-at-large, while British Ghanaian curator, author and art historian Osei Bonsu , Roma/Sinti curator and art historian Timea Junghaus and and Israeli curator and scholar Noam Segal were picked as the quinquennial’s curatorial advisors.

The four will work alongside Beckwith’s all-women team announced last year, composed of Carla Acevedo-Yates, Romi Crawford, Mayra A. Rodríguez Castro and Xiaoyu Weng.

Documenta 16 is scheduled to open 12 June 2027 through 19 September 2027.

title_original: Clare McAndrew on How to Measure the Art Market
editorial_title_zh: 克莱尔·麦克安德鲁谈如何衡量艺术市场
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位巴塞尔艺术展与瑞银集团艺术市场报告背后的经济学家，谈论了10年的数据分析、Z世代的消费支出，以及为什么收藏家在买藏品时选择走稳妥路线。

article_text:
For a decade, the Art Basel and UBS Art Market Report has been one of the most widely cited surveys about the market. In this extended episode of Art Market Minute, host Margaret Carrigan sits down with Clare McAndrew , founder of Arts Economics and the economist behind the report.

McAndrew traces her path from studying cultural economics to measuring the global art market, and explains what 10 years of data have taught her about how it behaves under pressure. The episode also digs into her latest research on collectors, published in the Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting , which finds that Gen Z is spending the most on fine art, more collectors are using A.I. tools for art-buying advice, and buyers are playing it safe with their purchases.
excerpt_original: The economist behind the Art Basel and UBS market report on 10 years of data analysis, Gen Z spending, and why collectors are playing it safe.
